# Real-Time Notification Service - Getting Started Guide ## Quick Setup (5 minutes) ### 1. Install Dependencies ```bash cd app/backend npm install ``` The following packages were added: - `@nestjs/websockets` and `@nestjs/socket.io` - WebSocket support - `socket.io` and `socket.io-redis` - Socket.IO with Redis adapter - `firebase-admin` - Firebase Cloud Messaging - `nodemailer` - Email sending ### 2. Configure Environment Variables Create or update `.env` file in `app/backend/`: ```env # Database DATABASE_PATH=./database.sqlite # Mail Configuration SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com SMTP_PORT=587 SMTP_SECURE=false SMTP_USER=your-email@gmail.com SMTP_PASSWORD=your-app-password EMAIL_FROM=noreply@gatheraa.com # Firebase (for push notifications) FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=your-project-id FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS={"type":"service_account",...full json...} # Redis (for pub/sub and scaling) REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 # JWT JWT_SECRET=your-secret-key-here # Server PORT=3000 NODE_ENV=development ``` ### 3. Start Redis (if running locally) ```bash # Using Docker docker run -d -p 6379:6379 redis:latest # Or if Redis installed locally redis-server ``` ### 4. Run Application ```bash npm run start:dev ``` ### 5. Verify Installation ```bash # Check health endpoint curl http://localhost:3000/notifications/health # Should return # {"status":"healthy"} ``` ## API Quick Test ### Create a Notification (REST) ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/notifications \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "type": "in_app", "category": "event_reminder", "title": "Test Notification", "message": "This is a test", "sendImmediately": true }' ``` ### Connect via WebSocket (JavaScript) ```javascript // In browser console or Node.js const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/notifications', { auth: { token: 'your-jwt-token' } }); socket.on('connection_established', (data) => { console.log('Connected:', data); }); socket.on('notification_received', (notification) => { console.log('New notification:', notification); }); // Get unread count socket.emit('get_unread_count'); socket.on('unread_count', (data) => { console.log('Unread count:', data.count); }); ``` ## Key Files to Review 1. **Core Service** - `src/notifications/notifications.service.ts` - Main notification logic 2. **WebSocket** - `src/notifications/gateway/notifications.gateway.ts` - Real-time events 3. **Entities** - `src/notifications/entities/` - Database schemas 4. **Tests** - `test/notifications.integration.spec.ts` - Integration tests 5. **Documentation** - `docs/NOTIFICATIONS_README.md` - Full API documentation - `NOTIFICATION_IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md` - Architecture overview ## Run Tests ```bash # All tests npm test # Notifications only npm test -- notifications # With coverage npm test:cov -- notifications # Integration tests npm run test:e2e -- notifications.integration.spec.ts ``` ## Common Integration Points ### In Reviews Module ```typescript // When a new review is created async createReview(dto: CreateReviewDto) { const review = await this.reviewRepository.save(/* ... */); // Notify organizer await this.notificationsService.sendReviewNotification(review, event); } ``` ### In Events Module ```typescript // When event is about to start async sendEventReminders() { const upcomingEvents = await this.eventsRepository.find({ where: { startsAt: between(now, now + 1 hour) } }); for (const event of upcomingEvents) { await this.notificationsService.sendBulkNotifications({ userIds: event.attendeeIds, types: [NotificationType.IN_APP, NotificationType.PUSH], category: NotificationCategory.EVENT_REMINDER, title: `${event.name} starts soon!`, message: `Your event starts in 1 hour`, metadata: { eventId: event.id } }); } } ``` ### In Ticket Sales ```typescript // When ticket is purchased async purchaseTicket(ticketId: string, userId: string) { const ticket = await this.ticketRepository.save(/* ... */); // Notify organizer await this.notificationsService.createAndSendNotification({ userId: ticket.event.organizerId, type: NotificationType.IN_APP, category: NotificationCategory.TICKET_SALE, title: 'Ticket Sold!', message: `${user.firstName} purchased a ticket`, metadata: { ticketId: ticket.id } }); } ``` ## Customization Guide ### Adding a New Notification Type 1. Add to `NotificationCategory` enum in `src/notifications/entities/notification.entity.ts`: ```typescript export enum NotificationCategory { // ... existing types ... CUSTOM_TYPE = 'custom_type', } ``` 2. Create default preferences in `PreferencesService.createDefaultPreferences()`: ```typescript categoryPreferences: { // ... existing ... customType: { email: true, push: true, inApp: true, sms: false }, } ``` 3. Use in your code: ```typescript await this.notificationsService.createAndSendNotification({ userId, type: NotificationType.IN_APP, category: NotificationCategory.CUSTOM_TYPE, title: 'Custom Notification', message: 'Your custom message' }); ``` ### Creating a Template ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/notifications/templates \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "code": "welcome_v1", "name": "Welcome Email", "description": "Sent when new user joins", "category": "system_alert", "emailSubject": "Welcome to Gatheraa, {{firstName}}!", "emailTemplate": "

Welcome {{firstName}}

We are excited to have you.

", "pushTitle": "Welcome!", "pushMessage": "Welcome to Gatheraa, {{firstName}}", "inAppTitle": "Welcome", "inAppMessage": "Welcome to the Gatheraa community!", "variables": ["firstName"] }' ``` ### Using a Template ```typescript const notification = await this.notificationsService.createAndSendNotification({ userId, type: NotificationType.EMAIL, category: NotificationCategory.SYSTEM_ALERT, title: 'Welcome Email', message: 'Welcome to Gatheraa', templateId: 'welcome_v1', // Uses welcome_v1 template data: { firstName: 'John' }, sendImmediately: true }); ``` ## Troubleshooting ### WebSocket Connection Failed **Problem**: WebSocket connection times out or fails **Solutions**: 1. Check JWT token is valid: ```bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" http://localhost:3000/auth/verify ``` 2. Check CORS settings in `main.ts` 3. Check Socket.IO is listening: ```bash curl http://localhost:3000/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling ``` ### Notifications Not Being Sent **Problem**: Notifications created but not visible **Solutions**: 1. Check user preferences are enabled: ```bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" http://localhost:3000/notifications/preferences/me ``` 2. Check Redis connection: ```bash redis-cli ping # Should return PONG ``` 3. Check email provider credentials in `.env` 4. Review logs for errors: ```bash npm run start:dev 2>&1 | grep -i notification ``` ### Rate Limit Errors **Problem**: Getting "Rate limit exceeded" errors **Solutions**: 1. Temporarily increase rate limit in `NotificationsService`: ```typescript private readonly DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT = 100; // Increase from 100 ``` 2. Or wait 1 hour for the rate limit window to reset ### Email Not Sending **Problem**: Email notifications stuck in queue **Solutions**: 1. body:
Implements #230. Adds:

## Changes

### Schema (src/db/schema.ts)
- New `oauth_tokens` table for per-user token storage (user_id, provider, email, refresh_token, scopes)
- UNIQUE constraint on (user_id, provider) for upsert support

### Multi-user OAuth (src/lib/gmail.ts + src/app.ts)
- `getGmailClientForUser(userId)` — creates authenticated Gmail client for a specific Slack user
- `getUserRefreshToken(userId)` — reads from oauth_tokens table
- `saveUserRefreshToken(userId, token, email?)` — upserts to oauth_tokens table
- `generateAuthUrlForUser(userId)` — embeds user_id in OAuth state parameter
- `/api/oauth/google/auth-url?user_id=U0678NQJ2` — generates user-specific auth URL
- `/api/oauth/google/callback` — parses state to route token to oauth_tokens (multi-user) or settings (default)
- Added `gmail.compose` scope for draft creation
- Full backward compatibility with existing aura@realadvisor.com token flow

### Draft Functions (src/lib/gmail.ts)
- `createDraft(userId, options)` — create a draft with full RFC 2822 support
- `listDrafts(userId, maxResults)` — list drafts with metadata
- `deleteDraft(userId, draftId)` — delete a specific draft

### Inbox Access (src/lib/gmail.ts)
- `readUserEmails(userId, options)` — read emails from any authorized user's inbox
- `readUserEmail(userId, messageId)` — read full email detail

### New Tools (src/tools/email.ts)
- `create_gmail_draft` — create a draft in a user's Gmail
- `list_gmail_drafts` — list drafts in a user's Gmail
- `read_user_emails` — read emails from a user's inbox
- `read_user_email` — read a specific email from a user's inbox

All tools resolve user_name → Slack user ID → OAuth token → Gmail API.

Built by Aura via sandbox code generation.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces new OAuth state validation, token storage, and user-scoped Gmail access paths; mistakes could expose or misuse per-user email access or break the existing OAuth callback behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **multi-user Gmail OAuth** support by introducing an `oauth_tokens` table and extending the OAuth flow to generate user-specific consent URLs (signed `state`) and persist refresh tokens per Slack `user_id`, while keeping the existing single-account `settings` token path as a fallback.
> 
> Extends Gmail capabilities to operate *on behalf of authorized users*: adds `gmail.compose` scope, supports fetching the authorized email during token exchange, and introduces user-scoped Gmail operations (draft create/list/delete and inbox read) surfaced as new Slack AI tools via `createGmailEATools()` and wired into the main Slack tool registry.

author: platorunner
body:
## Summary

Adds `"restart": true` to the `commands` section of the OpenClaw configuration template. This enables automatic gateway restarts when configuration files or skills are modified.

## What `restart: true` does

When enabled, OpenClaw automatically restarts the gateway service when:
- `openclaw.json` is modified
- Skills are added/updated/removed
- Plugin configuration changes

**Without it:** Users must manually run `openclaw gateway restart` after any config change
**With it:** Zero-downtime config reloads happen automatically

## Changes

- Added `"restart": true` to `commands` object in `do/openclaw.json.template`

## Note on existing settings

The template already includes `compaction: { mode: "safeguard" }` which prevents aggressive context pruning - good for preserving conversation continuity during long sessions.

## Related: `replace` vs `merge` mode

The template uses `"mode": "merge"` for models, which preserves OpenClaw's default providers while adding custom ones. This is different from `"replace"` mode which completely overrides defaults. For production:
- **merge** (current): Gets new default models automatically, may have surprise costs
- **replace**: Full control over available models, no surprise API calls

Consider documenting this trade-off in SETUP.md for users deciding between the two approaches.

author: pushpak1300
body:
MCP HTTP servers protected by OAuth 2.1 (per the [2025-11-25 spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization)) require a Bearer token on every request. Relay had no way to supply a per-request runtime token — only a static `api_key` in config — making per-user OAuth flows impossible.

### Usage

```php
// Caller handles the OAuth flow and obtains a token, then passes it to Relay:
$tools = Relay::withToken($user->mcp_token)->tools('github');

// Catch 401s to trigger re-authorization:
try {
    $tools = Relay::withToken($token)->tools('github');
} catch (AuthorizationException $e) {
    return redirect('/oauth/reconnect'); // token expired or rejected
}
```

### How the flow works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant App as Your Laravel App
    participant Relay
    participant MCP as MCP Server
    participant AS as Authorization Server

    Note over User,AS: Phase 1 — One-time OAuth setup (your app's responsibility)

    User->>App: Connect MCP account
    App->>MCP: GET /mcp (no token)
    MCP-->>App: 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="..."

    App->>MCP: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
    MCP-->>App: { authorization_servers: ["https://auth.example.com"] }

    App->>AS: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
    AS-->>App: { authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, ... }

    App->>User: Redirect to authorization URL (+ PKCE challenge + resource param)
    User->>AS: Log in & approve
    AS-->>App: Authorization code via redirect

    App->>AS: POST /token (code + PKCE verifier + resource)
    AS-->>App: { access_token, refresh_token }

    App->>App: Store tokens in DB (per user, per server)

    Note over User,AS: Phase 2 — Runtime tool use (Relay's responsibility)

    User->>App: Make a request that needs MCP tools
    App->>Relay: Relay::withToken($user->mcp_token)->tools('github')
    Relay->>MCP: POST /mcp tools/list\nAuthorization: Bearer <token>
    MCP-->>Relay: Tool definitions
    Relay-->>App: [Tool, Tool, Tool]

    App->>Relay: Prism calls a tool via handler
    Relay->>MCP: POST /mcp tools/call\nAuthorization: Bearer <token>
    MCP-->>Relay: Tool result
    Relay-->>App: "result string"

    Note over User,AS: Phase 3 — Token expiry (your app's responsibility)

    App->>Relay: Relay::withToken($expiredToken)->tools('github')
    Relay->>MCP: POST /mcp\nAuthorization: Bearer <expired>
    MCP-->>Relay: 401 Unauthorized
    Relay-->>App: throws AuthorizationException

    alt Has valid refresh token
        App->>AS: POST /token (refresh_token)
        AS-->>App: { new access_token, new refresh_token }
        App->>App: Save new tokens to DB
        App->>Relay: Relay::withToken($newToken)->tools('github')
        Relay->>MCP: POST /mcp (retried with new token)
        MCP-->>Relay: Tool definitions
        Relay-->>App: [Tool, Tool, Tool]
    else Refresh expired or revoked
        App->>User: Redirect to /oauth/reconnect (Phase 1 again)
    end
```

Your application is responsible for **Phase 1** (discovery, PKCE authorization code flow, token storage/refresh). Relay handles **Phase 2** — attaching `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to every MCP request and surfacing `AuthorizationException` on 401 so your app knows when to re-authorize.

Fixes #27

LAP DRAFT RACING のブラッシュアップ計画を実装。操作感改善からコア体験の追加、バグ修正、コードベースのリファクタリングまでを一貫して対応しました。

### Phase 0: 操作感改善
- **ドリフトシステム**: ハンドブレーキ＋ステアリングでドリフト発動、ブースト付与

- **壁衝突の段階的減速**: 接触回数に応じた減速（軽→中→重→ワープ）
- **コース固有効果**: 6 コースそれぞれに摩擦・速度補正（森の泥、山の坂、雪の滑り等）

### Phase 1: コア体験
- **ドラフトカードシステム**: ラップ完了時にカード 3 枚から 1 枚選択、14 種のカード効果
- **ハイライト検出**: ドリフトボーナス・HEAT ブースト・ニアミス回避・逆転・ファステストラップ・フォトフィニッシュの 6 種検出＋通知表示
- **リザルト画面強化**: ハイライトサマリー・ラップタイム・シェアボタン

- ゲームループ状態遷移バグ修正
- フィードバック第 1〜3 弾で計 14 件のバグ修正（壁ハマり・ゴースト・角ハマり・通知等）
- 6 機能追加（CPU ドリフト・モバイル対応・サウンド改善等）

### リファクタリング（SOLID/DRY/KISS）
- **RacingGame.tsx**: 1,257 行 → 752 行（-40%）に削減

  - `card-effects.ts` — カード効果乗算の DRY 共通関数

  - `game-update.ts` — 入力収集・パーティクル更新（SRP）
  - `game-draw.ts` — HUD/カウントダウン/通知描画（SRP）
  - `draft-ui-logic.ts` — ドラフト状態管理・遷移ロジック（SRP）
  - `components/MenuPanel.tsx` — メニュー UI コンポーネント
  - `components/ResultPanel.tsx` — リザルト UI コンポーネント
- **highlight.ts**: マジックナンバー定数化 + 内部ヘルパーで DRY 化
- **renderer.ts**: `renderDraftCard` 関数抽出
- **game-logic.ts**: 壁処理を `wall-physics.ts` に委譲

- **47 件 → 151 件**（+104 件）
- 新規テスト: drift / heat / course-effects / draft-cards / highlight / card-effects / wall-physics

## Summary

`asyncio.get_event_loop()` was deprecated in Python 3.10 when no running
loop exists, and raises `RuntimeError` in Python 3.14. This caused
`AsyncioConnection` to fail when instantiated from a non-async thread or
from a plain synchronous context where no event loop has been started.

## Changes

- Replace `asyncio.get_event_loop()` in `_AsyncioIOServicesAdapter.__init__`
  with `asyncio.get_running_loop()`, falling back to `asyncio.new_event_loop()`
  when no loop is running. This correctly reuses an existing running loop (e.g.
  when called from within async code) and safely creates a new one otherwise.
- Update the docstring in `AsyncioConnection.__init__` to reflect the new
  behaviour.
- Remove the `try/except get_event_loop()` workaround in
  `io_services_test_stubs_test.py` that was masking the same issue in the
  test suite.
- Add `tests/unit/asyncio_connection_tests.py` covering all three code paths:
  explicit loop, running loop reuse, and new loop creation when none is running
  (both from a thread and from a plain synchronous context).

## Related

Closes #1479

## Types of Changes

What types of changes does your code introduce to this project? Put an x in the boxes that apply

- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes issue #1479)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

author: copilot
body:
`PROGRESSION_RE` requires 3+ consecutive whitespace-separated chord tokens. Pipe characters in bar notation break that sequence — `| Fmaj7   | Em      | A       |` produces runs of 1 chord between each `|`, falling below the detection threshold.

## Changes

- **`isBarNotationLine(line)`** — new predicate that returns `true` when a line's only non-whitespace content (after stripping `|`) consists entirely of valid chord tokens. Empty bars like `|  |    |  |    |` return `false`.

- **Normalization pass in `replaceInPage()`** — when a text node contains `|`, bar-notation lines are pre-processed (pipes → spaces) before `PROGRESSION_RE` runs:

  ```
  | Fmaj7   | Em      | A       |
  →   Fmaj7     Em       A        ← now matched by PROGRESSION_RE
  ```

- **DOM write condition** updated from `newValue !== original` to `newValue !== normalized` — the node is only mutated when a chord transformation actually occurred, not merely because pipes were stripped.

`js/app.js` was deleted in a prior PR (superseded by `js/scripts.js`), but the three standalone auth pages retain `<script src="/js/app.js">` tags that reference the now-missing file, causing 404s on login, register, and logout.

## Changes

- **`app/views/auth/login.php`** — removed `<script src="/js/app.js" defer></script>`
- **`app/views/auth/register.php`** — removed `<script src="/js/app.js"></script>`
- **`app/views/auth/logout.php`** — removed `<script src="/js/app.js"></script>`

These pages use a standalone HTML structure (not the main layout), so they carried their own script includes. They require no JavaScript functionality, so the tags are simply removed.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem
> 
> There are three JavaScript files that all define the same global functions (`initAlerts`, `apiCall`, `showAlert`, `confirmAction`, modal management), causing duplicate event listeners and conflicts:
> 
> 1. `js/app.js` — defines `initAlerts`, `apiCall`, `showAlert`, `confirmAction`, and registers its own `DOMContentLoaded` listener
> 2. `js/scripts.js` — redefines **all the same functions** plus adds modal management (`initModals`, `openModal`, `closeModal`, `closeAllModals`, `window.modalManager`) and navigation (`initNavigation`). This is the most complete and correct version.
> 3. `js/modals.js` — duplicates the modal management code from `scripts.js` but with a worse implementation (registers a separate `keydown` listener per modal instead of a single document-level listener)
> 
> In `app/views/layouts/main.php`, both `app.js` and `scripts.js` are loaded (lines 10-11):
> ```html
> <script src="/js/app.js" defer></script>
> <script src="/js/scripts.js" defer></script>
> ```
> 
> This causes:
> - `initAlerts` running twice (once from each file's `DOMContentLoaded`)
> - `apiCall` and `showAlert` being defined twice with slightly different error handling (app.js silently swallows parse errors as `{success: true}`, while scripts.js correctly reports them)
> - Duplicate global function definitions overwriting each other
> 
> ## Required Changes
> 
> 1. **Delete `js/app.js`** — it is fully superseded by `scripts.js`. The `scripts.js` version has better error handling in `apiCall` (reports parse errors instead of silently returning `{success: true}`).
> 
> 2. **Delete `js/modals.js`** — it is fully superseded by the modal management code in `scripts.js`. The `scripts.js` version is better because it uses a single document-level escape key listener with a guard flag (`escapeListenerAdded`) instead of adding one listener per modal.
> 
> 3. **Remove the `<script src="/js/app.js" defer></script>` line from `app/views/layouts/main.php`** (line 10). Do NOT remove the `scripts.js` script tag.
> 
> 4. **Do NOT modify `js/scripts.js`** — it already contains all the needed functionality and is correct as-is.
> 
> After these changes, `scripts.js` will be the single JavaScript file handling alerts, API calls, modals, and navigation.


</details>

author: martbeat
body:
### Motivation
- Avoid corrupting DOCX layout/markup when performing redaction by replacing raw XML-wide string substitution with a text-node-aware approach that preserves WordprocessingML structure.
- Ensure XML entities (e.g. `&`, `'`) are handled consistently between DOCX extraction and export to avoid incorrect decoding/encoding of content such as apostrophes.
- Improve user control and reliability of the in-browser pipeline (extraction → detection → export) with clearer UI controls and fallbacks for CDN-loaded libraries.

### Description
- Added XML helpers `decodeXmlText` and `encodeXmlText` and a dedicated `redactWordProcessingMlText(xml, selectedValues, maskToken)` function that only rewrites `<w:t>` text node content, preserving surrounding WordprocessingML markup.
- Replaced naive global DOCX string replacement with processing that updates common WordprocessingML parts (`word/document.xml`, headers, footers, footnotes, endnotes, comments) and uses the configured mask token via `getMaskToken()`.
- Reused `decodeXmlText` in `extractTextFromDocx()` for consistent entity decoding and improved handling of apostrophes; updated export status messaging to note split-run caveats.
- Added UI and pipeline improvements: `maskToken` input, `Run all` pipeline button, findings filter, visible/selected counts, drag-and-drop support, `Ctrl+Enter` shortcut, broadened detectors (names, URLs, phones, dates, financial/gov/IP heuristics) and a dependency loader with CDN fallbacks for `pdfjs`, `jsPDF`, and `JSZip`.

### Testing
- Started a local HTTP server with `python -m http.server 8130 --bind 0.0.0.0` and loaded the modified `redactor.html` to serve the page for in-browser tests (succeeded).
- Ran an automated Playwright (Firefox) in-page function test that invoked `redactWordProcessingMlText(...)` on a representative WordprocessingML sample containing entities and apostrophes and verified the expected targets were redacted while surrounding XML remained intact (succeeded).

body:
### Motivation
- The visual style selector only updated the local page instance, causing the layout/footer to remain out of sync until a refresh or remount.
- Changing the style should immediately affect all mounted consumers (Store page, Layout/footer, Starter/etc.) and sync across tabs.

### Description
- Reworked `useVisualStyle` (`src/hooks/useVisualStyle.ts`) to use a global in-memory snapshot + subscription model instead of per-hook `useState` so updates propagate instantly to all subscribers.
- Switched to `useSyncExternalStore` so components read the shared snapshot and re-render when `setStyle` calls `setGlobalStyle`.
- Persisted the chosen style to `localStorage` and added a `storage` event listener in the subscription so cross-tab changes stay in sync.
- Kept the public hook API unchanged: it still returns `{ style, setStyle, styleClassName }` for minimal changes across the codebase.

### Testing
- Built the app with `npm run build` and the production build completed successfully.
- Ran `npm run lint`, which reported unrelated existing repo lint issues (no new lint failures from this change).
- Launched the dev server and executed an automated Playwright script that simulated selecting a style in the Store and captured a screenshot showing the Store and footer updated; screenshot artifact confirmed the fix.

author: madmax983
body:
# 🌟 Nova: Tooling API - Execute Anonymous Apex

## The Spark 🔭
I noticed we have a robust REST and Bulk API client, but we lack the ability to "script" Salesforce or perform developer-centric tasks. The `tooling` feature flag existed in `Cargo.toml` but was unimplemented.

## The Feature 🚀
I've implemented the **Tooling API**, starting with the **Execute Anonymous** resource.
This allows developers to run arbitrary Apex code from Rust, opening the door for:
-   **Scripting:** Automate complex data setups or cleanups that are hard to do via REST.
-   **Debugging:** rapid prototyping of Apex logic.
-   **CI/CD:** Triggering batch classes or system checks.

## The Potential 🔮
This is the first step into the Tooling API. We can expand this to support:
-   Querying `ApexClass`, `ApexTrigger`, `TraceFlag`.
-   Retrieving Code Coverage.
-   Compiling Apex (eventually).

## Implementation Details
-   New module: `crates/force/src/api/tooling/mod.rs`.
-   New method: `client.tooling().execute_anonymous("System.debug('Hello');")`.
-   Returns a structured `ExecuteAnonymousResult` with compile/runtime error details.
-   Isolated behind the `tooling` feature flag.

## Risk ⚠️
Low. The feature is additive and gated. Core logic is untouched (except for exposing the new module).
I also fixed a pre-existing documentation warning in `composite_batch.rs` while I was in the neighborhood.

author: madmax983
body:
Identified a potential integer overflow in the SIMD implementation of `draw_scanline_phong_shadowed_simd` (and likely others) where signed 32-bit offsets are used for memory gather instructions. If a `ZBuffer` exceeds `i32::MAX` elements (approx 2.14 billion), the index calculation wraps to negative, accessing invalid memory.

This change enforces a strict limit of `i32::MAX` pixels in `ZBuffer::new`, aligning it with the existing `Texture` implementation and ensuring safe SIMD execution. A regression test `tests/verify_zbuffer_limit.rs` was added to verify the fix.

Also fixed a minor Clippy warning in `src/rasterizer/reflection.rs`.

author: rebkwok
body:
Measures denominator value can be big.  E.g. [this measure](https://github.com/opensafely/raw_medicines_short_data_report/blob/902b4f4136391e308d3a819af3f46db856f621a5/analysis/measures_definition.py#L81) calculates the number of medications in an interval over all medications, which is >10b and results in an Arithmentic Overflow error in the mssql engine.

To avoid this, we cast the denominator column to BIGINT before summing. There's no easy way to tell if it needs to be a bigint in advance, so we need to do this for all denominators. Numerators are unlkely to be bigger than ~2b, so leave them as the default int.

Also removes the unnecessary group by and grouping sets where there are no groups. I'm not sure if this has any impact on the efficiency of the query but it makes the SQL more complex, and it's quite simple to avoid it.

- **Drug Interaction & Allergy Checker (US3 — P2)**: 40+ curated drug interaction pairs + fuzzy allergy matching; auto-alerts on MAJOR/CONTRAINDICATED findings
- **Clinical Alerts Feed (US4 — P2)**: Unified paginated alert feed with acknowledge/dismiss actions; global and per-patient views; full RBAC
- **Patient Risk Dashboard (US5 — P2)**: Risk-ranked patient table (critical alerts → NEWS2 score → warnings) + system-wide stats snapshot

## Technical Highlights

- 3 new Flyway migrations (V22–V24): `lab_orders`, `lab_results`, `clinical_alerts` tables with UUID PKs
- `DrugInteractionDatabase` — static `@Component` bean with 40+ clinically significant drug pairs (no external API)
- Alert deduplication — service-layer logic ensures only one ACTIVE NEWS2 alert per `(patientId, alertType)` at a time
- Full audit logging on all mutations (lab orders, results, alert status changes)
- Frontend: 7 new React pages/components — `ClinicalAlertsFeedPage`, `PatientRiskDashboardPage`, `News2ScoreCard`, `AlertFeed`, `LabOrderList`, `RiskDashboardTable`; auto-refresh every 30s via `refetchInterval`

- Role matrix coverage: DOCTOR / NURSE / ADMIN / RECEPTIONIST for every endpoint

author: mushuiyu422
body:
Previously, the before_agent_start hook's systemPrompt return value was collected but never actually merged into the session's system prompt. This prevented extensions like memory-flex from injecting user profiles and memories into the AI model's system context. Changes: - Change systemPromptText from const to let to allow modification - Call before_agent_start hook before createAgentSession - Merge hookResult.systemPrompt into systemPromptText if provided - Add debug logging for successful systemPrompt injection - Add error handling for hook failures This enables memory-flex and other extensions to inject context into the system prompt that affects model behavior without appearing in the user-visible message list. Fixes the issue where before_agent_start hook's systemPrompt was ignored, requiring post-build patching scripts for bundled versions. Linked Issue/PR Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8176

Greptile Summary

Fixed a critical bug where the `before_agent_start` hook's `systemPrompt` return value was collected but never merged into the agent session's system prompt. The hook is now executed before `createAgentSession` and its `systemPrompt` is properly appended to `systemPromptText`, enabling extensions like memory-flex to inject context. Key changes in `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.ts`: - Changed `systemPromptText` from `const` to `let` to allow modification - Moved `before_agent_start` hook execution before session creation (line 606-634) - Appended hook's `systemPrompt` to `systemPromptText` with proper validation - Cached the hook result to avoid duplicate execution - Added error handling with warning logs The README.md change adds markdownlint disable/enable comments around the sponsors HTML table. The msteams test change converts local file paths to `file://` URLs for cross-platform consistency and adds the optional `sharePointSiteId` parameter (set to undefined).

Confidence Score: 5/5

- This PR is safe to merge with minimal risk - The changes are well-structured and address a clear bug. The implementation correctly moves hook execution before session creation, properly validates and merges the systemPrompt, includes error handling, and caches the result to prevent duplicate execution. The test changes are benign improvements for cross-platform compatibility. - No files require special attention Last reviewed commit: b81fb74

Complete rebranding from "FinançasPro" to "CromaHub - Finanças" with a new inline SVG logo, updated color palette, and a series of functional bug fixes targeting numeric field editing, mobile layout overflow, and transaction form UX. ## Rebranding - **New `CromaHubLogo.tsx`** — inline SVG with abstract molecule/orbital geometry, blue→purple gradient (`#1FA6FF`→`#2A1FCE`), "CROMA" in gradient + "HUB" in solid text; accepts `size` and `showText` props - **`Layout.tsx`** — sidebar + mobile header replace text brand with `` - **`Login.tsx` / `Register.tsx`** — replace `Wallet` icon with logo, background → deep dark `#0a0a1a`, submit button uses brand gradient - **`index.css`** — CSS variables updated (`--accent-primary: #1FA6FF`, dark `--bg-*` to `#0a0a1a`/`#0d1117`/`#141428`); `overflow-x: hidden` added to `html, body, #root` - **`App.css`** — removed `max-width: 1280px` constraint on `#root` ## Numeric field editing (bug 2.2) Fields like credit limit, closing day, balance, and amount previously snapped back to `0` on clear. Fixed by storing values as strings, converting only on submit: ```tsx // Cards.tsx — was: closing_day: parseInt(e.target.value) || 1 onChange={(e) => setFormData({ ...formData, closing_day: e.target.value })} // handleSubmit: closing_day: parseInt(String(formData.closing_day)) || 1 ``` ## Default + primary account (bugs 2.3 & 2.4) - **`authController.ts`** — creates a `Conta Principal` (corrente, balance=0, `is_primary=1`) on user registration - **`database.ts`** — migration adds `is_primary INTEGER DEFAULT 0` to `bank_accounts` - **`accountController.ts`** — new `setPrimaryAccount` handler: clears all `is_primary` flags for user, sets target account - **`routes/accounts.ts`** — `PUT /:id/set-primary` wired up - **`Accounts.tsx`** — star icon button to toggle primary; filled/outlined based on `account.is_primary` - **`Transactions.tsx`** — pre-selects primary account on data load ## Transaction form UX (bugs 2.5 & 2.6) - **Hide "Conta" when payment is Cartão de Crédito** — wrapped account selector in `{formData.payment_method !== 'cartao' && (...)}` - **Fix stray "0" below card selector** — `is_shared` comes back as SQLite integer `0`; `{... && card.is_shared && ...}` was rendering `0` as text; fixed with `!!`: ```tsx // was: cards.find(...)?.is_shared && !!cards.find(c => c.id === formData.card_id)?.is_shared && ( ``` ## Recurring expenses (bug 2.7) Pay/unpay toggle button now renders `Pagar` / `Pago` alongside the check icon for clarity.
Original prompt ## Contexto Este é um sistema financeiro pessoal construído com React (frontend em `frontend/src/`) e Express/Node.js (backend em `backend/src/`). O site precisa de um rebranding completo e diversas correções de bugs, especialmente no mobile. ## 1. Rebranding para "CromaHub - Finanças" ### 1.1 Nome do site - Alterar TODAS as referências do nome atual para **"CromaHub - Finanças"** em todo o projeto - O `` da página HTML (em `frontend/index.html`) deve ser "CromaHub - Finanças" - Alterar o nome no sidebar/layout (`frontend/src/components/Layout.tsx`), login (`frontend/src/pages/Login.tsx`), register e qualquer outro lugar ### 1.2 Logo SVG inline Como não temos o arquivo de imagem da logo, criar um **componente SVG inline** (`frontend/src/components/CromaHubLogo.tsx`) que represente a logo com as seguintes características: - **Símbolo**: Formas geométricas abstratas com ovais/círculos conectados por curvas suaves, lembrando moléculas/conexões digitais - **Cores do símbolo**: Degradê de azul claro vibrante (`#1FA6FF`) até azul escuro/roxo (`#2A1FCE`) - **Texto "CROMA"**: Em degradê azul→roxo, fonte robusta e moderna - **Texto "HUB"**: Em preto/carvão (`#1a1a2e` para dark mode usar branco), fonte forte e sólida - O componente deve aceitar props de tamanho (`size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`) e `showText?: boolean` - Usar este componente na tela de login, no sidebar, e onde mais fizer sentido ### 1.3 Paleta de cores (tema do site) Atualizar a paleta de cores do site inteiro para combinar com a logo. Modificar os arquivos CSS (`frontend/src/index.css`, `frontend/src/App.css`) e as classes Tailwind inline nos componentes: - **Primary**: Degradê de `#1FA6FF` (azul claro) → `#2A1FCE` (azul/roxo) - **Background dark**: `#0a0a1a` ou `#0d1117` (escuro profundo) - **Cards/surfaces dark**: `#141428` ou `#161b22` - **Accent**: `#1FA6FF` (azul vibrante) - **Hover/Active states**: usar tons entre `#1FA6FF` e `#2A1FCE` - Substituir referências a `blue-600`, `blue-800` etc. para usar as novas cores da marca - Os botões primários devem usar o degradê da marca - O sidebar deve ter o gradiente sutil da marca - Manter bom contraste para legibilidade ## 2. Correções de Bugs ### 2.1 Dados não aparecem no mobile em certas abas **Problema**: As abas Agenda, Vendas (Orders), Orçamentos (Quotes), Estoque (Inventory) e Clientes aparecem no mobile, mas os **dados cadastrados não são exibidos** (a lista fica vazia mesmo tendo dados). **Causa provável**: Essas páginas usam `localStorage` com chaves como `finances_events`, `finances_clients`, `finances_orders`, `finances_quotes`, `finances_inventory_items`. O problema pode ser: - Overflow CSS escondendo o conteúdo no mobile - Cards/listas com largura fixa que saem da tela - O container da lista pode ter `overflow: hidden` cortando os itens **Solução**: - Verificar cada uma dessas páginas (`Agenda.tsx`, `Orders.tsx`, `Quotes.tsx`, `Clients.tsx` e Inventory se existir) e garantir que os cards de listagem usem `w-full`, `overflow-x-auto` quando necessário, e que nenhum elemento fixo esconda o conteúdo - Remover larguras fixas (`w-[500px]` etc.) e substituir por responsivas (`w-full max-w-lg` etc.) ### 2.2 Campos numéricos não permitem apagar o valor **Problema**: Campos como "dia de vencimento", "valor", "limite de crédito" não permitem apagar o 0 para digitar outro número. Ao tentar excluir, o 0 volta automaticamente. **Arquivos afetados**: `Cards.tsx` (closing_day, due_day, credit_limit), `Accounts.tsx` (balance), `Transactions.tsx` (amount) e qualquer outro formulário com campos numéricos. **Solução**: - Mudar campos numéricos para usar `type="text"` com `inputMode="numeric"` OU manter como `type="number"` mas tratar o estado como `string` (permitindo string vazia `''`) - Converter para número apenas no momento do submit - Nos handlers de `onChange`, permitir valor vazio: `setFormData({...formData, field: e.target.value === '' ? '' : e.target.value})` ### 2.3 Conta padrão para novos usuários **Problema**: Sem conta criada, o saldo geral no dashboard não atualiza. **Solução**: No backend (`backend/src/`), quando um usuário é registrado (rota de register), criar automaticamente uma conta "Conta Principal" do tipo "corrente" com saldo 0. Adicionar campo `is_primary` (BOOLEAN DEFAULT 0) na tabela de contas. A conta primária deve ser a padrão selecionada em formulários de transação. ### 2.4 Conta "principal" selecionável **Solução**: - No frontend `Accounts.tsx`, adicionar um botão/ícone de estrela para marcar uma conta como "principal" - No backend, criar endpoint `PUT /accounts/:id/set-primary` - Em `Transactions.tsx`, pré-selecionar a conta marcada como principal no `formData.account_id` ### 2.5 Esconder campo "Conta" quando "Cartão de Crédito" é selecionado **Problema**: No modal "Nova Transação" (`Transactions.tsx`), quando o método de pagamento é "Cartão de Crédito" (`cartao`), o campo de seleção de conta bancária ainda aparece (conforme screenshot). **Solução**: Adicio... </details> <!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX --> *This pull request was created from Copilot chat.* > <!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT TIPS --> --- 🔒 GitHub Advanced Security automatically protects Copilot coding agent pull requests. body:
## Summary

- Forward-mode dual numbers (`Dual<F>`) with all 30+ elemental operations and correct derivative rules
- Reverse-mode AD (`Reverse<F>`) with an Adept-style two-stack tape — precomputed partial derivatives, no opcode dispatch, single multiply-accumulate reverse sweep with zero-adjoint skipping
- Thread-local tape with RAII guard so `Reverse<F>` is `Copy` (12 bytes for f64)
- `Scalar` trait for AD-generic code: `fn f<T: Scalar>(x: T) -> T` works with `f64`, `Dual<f64>`, and `Reverse<f64>`

- Constant sentinel (`u32::MAX`) avoids tape bloat from literal values

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a complete Phase 7 Human Interface & Experience Layer that exposes the full UCI surface to humans via a beautiful, responsive, dependency-free web SPA and a stdlib HTTP API.
- Use only Python stdlib on the server-side (`http.server`) and vanilla HTML/CSS/JS on the frontend so the UI can run in standalone demo mode or connect to a real UCI backend through connectors.
- Offer full, read/write integration points for all previous phases (status, goals, capabilities, plans, construction, improvements, safety, settings, knowledge, notifications, timeline, health, console) while leaving existing phase code unchanged.
- Provide a self-contained standalone demo mode with mock data and a realtime simulation feed for interactive validation and UX testing.

### Description
- Added a new `frontend_system/` package implementing the Phase 7 layer, including an stdlib `http.server` based web server `UCIWebServer` (served by `frontend_system/server/web_server.py`) and an `APIRouter` that dispatches API requests to handler modules under `server/api_handlers/` (goals, status, capabilities, plans, construction, improvements, safety, settings, knowledge, notifications, timeline, health, console and base handler).
- Implemented middleware (`auth_middleware.py`, `cors_middleware.py`, `logging_middleware.py`, `safety_middleware.py`), static/template resolver (`static_handler.py`), a websocket-like long-poll scaffold (`websocket_handler.py`) and session manager (`session_manager.py`).
- Built a vanilla SPA frontend under `frontend_system/static/` and `frontend_system/templates/` including dark-theme CSS, reusable UI components, simple chart utilities, client router, API client, and one JS view module per required view (`dashboard`, `goals`, `capabilities`, `plans`, `construction`, `improvements`, `safety`, `console`, `settings`, `knowledge`, `notifications`, `timeline`, `health`).
- Implemented integration helpers in `frontend_system/integration/`: a `UCIConnector` (full method surface, returns mock data if no intelligence core provided), `RealtimeFeed` (long-poll / server-sent-like feed), `DataTransformer` (frontend-friendly JSON shaping), and lightweight `phase_connectors/` for each prior phase.
- Added `frontend_system/main.py` supporting `--standalone` (mock data + simulated realtime activity) and `--connect` modes, startup banner, lifecycle management, and automatic browser open for demo.
- Kept all changes isolated to the new `frontend_system/` package and added a simple demo integration layer (mock connectors) so the UI works without modifying existing Phase 0–6 code.

### Testing
- Compiled the new package tree with `python -m compileall frontend_system`, which completed successfully with no syntax errors.
- Launched the frontend in standalone demo mode and exercised API/static endpoints using automated checks: started server with `python -m frontend_system.main --standalone` and verified responses for `GET /api/status/dashboard`, `GET /api/goals`, and `GET /` (root HTML) using `curl`; responses returned expected JSON/HTML and server logs show requests handled successfully.

author: oaris-dev
body:
## Summary

- Fix permanent loading skeleton on share page when AI API keys are not configured
- Simplify `shouldShowLoading()` and polling logic: only show loading when `aiGenerationStatus` is explicitly `QUEUED` or `PROCESSING`

## Root Cause

When self-hosting without `GROQ_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`, the server never triggers AI generation, so `aiGenerationStatus` stays `null`. But the client-side `shouldShowLoading()` treated `null` status + no AI data as "still loading," causing an infinite skeleton.

The server-side `getVideoStatus` already handles this correctly — when it can't trigger generation (no API keys), it returns `aiGenerationStatus: null`. The client just needs to trust that `null` means "not happening."

## Changes

- `apps/web/app/s/[videoId]/Share.tsx`: Simplified both `shouldShowLoading()` and the polling `shouldContinuePolling()` to only return `true` when status is `QUEUED` or `PROCESSING`

## Test plan

- [ ] Self-host without AI keys → no loading skeleton below video
- [ ] Self-host with AI keys → skeleton shows during processing, disappears when complete
- [ ] Existing Cap.so behavior unchanged (aiGenerationEnabled gates the loading)

Closes #3

author: countercheck
body:
## Summary

- Adds an **Arbiter resolution strategy** as an alternative to Token Draw. A host-designated arbiter reviews player arguments, marks each as strong or weak, then rolls 2d6 (modified by strong argument counts) to produce a binary SUCCESS_BUT (+1) or FAILURE_BUT (−1) outcome.
- Introduces a new `ARBITER_REVIEW` game phase (between Argumentation and Resolution), a `GamePlayerRole` enum on `game_players`, and an `isStrong` flag on arguments — all backed by a database migration.
- Extracts resolution logic into a self-registering strategy pattern (`resolution/strategies/`) using cryptographically secure randomness, with a shared `random.ts` utility reused by both strategies.

## What changed

### Schema & migration
- New `GamePlayerRole` enum (`PLAYER` | `ARBITER`) on `game_players.game_role`
- New `ARBITER_REVIEW` value in `GamePhase` enum
- New `arguments.is_strong` boolean (default false)

### Server
- `arbiter.service.ts` — `markArgumentStrong()` toggles `isStrong`; `completeArbiterReview()` counts strong args, calls strategy, transitions to RESOLUTION
- `game.service.ts` — `setPlayerRole()` lets the host assign/revoke the ARBITER role; blocked during active phases (ARGUMENTATION → NARRATION)
- `arbiter.strategy.ts` — 2d6 roll via `rollDie()`, `modified = base + strongPro − strongAnti`, threshold > 7
- `random.ts` — shared `getSecureRandomInt` (rejection sampling) and `rollDie` used by both strategies

### Client
- `ArbiterReviewPhase.tsx` — arbiter sees grouped FOR/AGAINST arguments with toggle buttons; shows dice result after completion
- `ArbiterResolution.tsx` — result display: roll breakdown, modifiers, outcome
- `GameSidebar.tsx` — shows arbiter name and phase guide entry for ARBITER_REVIEW
- `GameView.tsx` — routes to `ArbiterReviewPhase` during `ARBITER_REVIEW` phase

### Tests
- `arbiter.service.test.ts` — authorization, phase guards, argument toggle, resolution flow
- `game-role.test.ts` — 14 tests: host-only, duplicate arbiter prevention, all 5 blocked phases
- `arbiter.strategy.test.ts` — boundary at modified=7, modifier math, metadata
- `random.test.ts` — range validation, input guards, distribution coverage

## Test plan

- [ ] Start a new game and set resolution method to `arbiter` in game settings
- [ ] Host assigns a player as Arbiter via the sidebar role control
- [ ] Create an action proposal and submit arguments from multiple players
- [ ] Advance to ARBITER_REVIEW — confirm non-arbiter players see "Waiting for [arbiter] to review"
- [ ] As arbiter, mark some arguments as Strong; confirm toggle persists on refresh
- [ ] Click "Complete Review & Roll Dice" — confirm transition to RESOLUTION with dice breakdown visible
- [ ] Verify result is SUCCESS_BUT or FAILURE_BUT (never TRIUMPH/DISASTER)
- [ ] Confirm host cannot reassign ARBITER role while in ARBITER_REVIEW (should get an error)
- [ ] Run `pnpm test` — all 812 server + 359 client tests pass
- [ ] Run `pnpm db:migrate` on a fresh DB — migration applies cleanly

author: gdsanger
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/gdsanger/Agira/security/code-scanning/151](https://github.com/gdsanger/Agira/security/code-scanning/151)

In general, the fix is to **avoid returning raw exception messages to the client**. Instead, log the detailed exception on the server (as is already done with `logger.error(..., exc_info=True)`) and send back a generic, non-sensitive error message. Where possible, reserve specific, user-friendly messages for expected/handled error types (like `ValidationError`) and keep truly unexpected errors generic.

For this specific code:

- Keep the existing logging in the `except Exception as e` block at line 10214 so that developers still see the full stack trace and message in server logs.
- Change the JSON response so that it does **not** include `str(e)`. Instead, use a generic message such as `"An unexpected error occurred while saving the blueprint."` or a similarly neutral text that does not reveal internals.
- We do not need new imports or additional methods: we can re-use the existing `logger` and `JsonResponse`.
- Only the `JsonResponse` construction on line 10216 needs to be changed accordingly.
- The analogous error handler in `blueprint_delete` (lines 10246–10248) already returns a generic message, so we will make `blueprint_update` consistent with that.

Concretely: in `core/views.py`, inside `blueprint_update`, replace

```python
return JsonResponse({'success': False, 'error': str(e)}, status=500)
```

with something like

```python
return JsonResponse(
    {
        'success': False,
        'error': 'An unexpected error occurred while saving the blueprint.'
    },
    status=500
)
```

This preserves behavior (error still indicated, status still 500) but removes exposure of exception text.

author: rad-vrc
body:
## 概要
モバイル環境（スマートフォン等）におけるパフォーマンス指標（LCP、TBT、INP）の大幅な改善と、ユーザビリティの向上を目的とした最適化を行いました。
Lighthouseのパフォーマンステストにて、モバイルでの大幅なスコアアップ（TBTの削減）を確認しています。

## 主な変更点

### 1. メインスレッドのブロック時間 (TBT) の劇的な削減
モバイル端末の弱いCPUでは、多数のリッチなCSS無限アニメーション（背景グラデーションの動き、浮遊エフェクト、重いドロップシャドウ等）が同時に実行されることでブラウザの計算リソースが枯渇し、タップ反応などが遅れる問題（TBT/INP悪化）が発生していました。
- **対応:** CSSのメディアクエリ (`@media (max-width: 768px)`) を用いて、モバイル閲覧時のみ重い無限アニメーションやフィルター処理を停止する最適化を行いました。（※ホバーやタップ時のアニメーションは維持しています）
- **結果:** LCP要素描画後のスタイル計算コストが大幅に下がり、画面のサクサク感が向上しました。

### 2. 初期レンダリング枚数の最適化 (Hydration Mismatch回避)
- SSR（サーバーサイドレンダリング）時にPCとモバイルで出力に差が出るとHydrationエラーやCLS（ガタつき）が起きるため、初期のレンダリング数を**モバイル環境にあわせた12枚(`MOBILE_RENDER_LIMIT`)**に統一しました。
- PC環境ではマウント直後に20枚(`DESKTOP_RENDER_LIMIT`)へ動的に追加描画されます。これにより、モバイルでの初期負荷を最小限に抑えつつ安定した描画を実現しています。

### 3. モバイル向けUI・レイアウトの微調整
- **VRChatリンクボタンの大幅拡大:** モバイル画面でのタップ領域を広げるため、サイズをPCの約1.8倍（95px相当）まで拡大し、少し左へ寄せて配置間隔を最適化しました。
- **三面図DLボタンのデザイン統一:** モバイルでも「三面図DL」のテキストラベルを省略せずに極小文字として表示し、アイコンも1.35倍に拡大してPCライクな比率で押しやすいように改善しました。
- **ロゴ画像のLCP最適化見直し:** Cloudflare Pagesの画像ローダー環境下において `unoptimized` プロパティが外れると正常にパス解決されない不具合が発生したため、すでに十分に軽量(約20KB)な元画像へ `unoptimized={true}` を再設定して安定稼働させました。

### 指標の改善結果 (Lighthouse モバイル計測)
- **TBT (Total Blocking Time):** （最適化前）2000ms超 → （最適化後）約500ms台へ大幅減
- 無駄なアニメーション描画（Style & Layout処理）によるCPU100%の張り付きが解消しました。

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure Norway uses Bonnetid as authoritative source for prayer times (month-level data) while keeping Aladhan unchanged for the rest of the world.
- Avoid exposing the Bonnetid API token in the browser and avoid per-day/timezone/date-shift bugs that caused off-by-one / minute mismatches in the monthly calendar.

### Description
- Added a secure Netlify proxy function `netlify/functions/bonnetid.ts` that forwards only whitelisted `?path=/...` requests to `https://api.bonnetid.no` and injects `Api-Token` read from `process.env.BONNETID_API_TOKEN` (with `BONNETID_API_KEY` fallback); CORS headers are returned for the app.

author: gdsanger
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/gdsanger/Agira/security/code-scanning/149](https://github.com/gdsanger/Agira/security/code-scanning/149)

In general, the fix is to avoid returning raw exception information to the client. Instead, log the detailed exception (including stack trace) on the server, and send a generic, non-sensitive error message in the HTTP response. This way, developers keep full diagnostics in logs, while clients get a safe and predictable error payload.

For this specific code, we should modify the `except Exception as e:` block in `change_policy_update` so that it no longer includes `str(e)` in the JSON. The call to `logger.error(..., exc_info=True)` is good and should remain. The `JsonResponse` should instead return a fixed, generic message like `"An unexpected error occurred while updating the change policy."` or similar. This does not change control flow or the response structure (`{'success': False, 'error': ...}`), so clients can continue to rely on the same keys, just with a safer message value.

Concretely:
- In `core/views.py`, locate the `change_policy_update` view’s `except Exception as e:` block (lines 9960–9962).
- Keep the `logger.error` call as-is.
- Replace `JsonResponse({'success': False, 'error': str(e)}, status=500)` with a `JsonResponse` that uses a generic error message string instead of `str(e)`.
- No new imports or helper methods are required.

## Summary

Closes #130

- Adds a `group` metadata key on sessions with `Group()`/`SetGroup()` convenience accessors
- Adds `tui.group_by` config option (`"repo"` default, `"group"` for custom grouping)
- Adds `GroupSet` action type with `G` keybinding — opens a text input to set/clear a session's group

author: pyaethu-aung
body:
## Summary

Resolves 4 high-severity vulnerabilities reported by `npm audit --audit-level=high`, caused by a ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service) vulnerability in `minimatch < 10.2.1`.

Fixes: [GHSA-3ppc-4f35-3m26](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3ppc-4f35-3m26)

## Root Cause

`eslint@9.x` transitively pulled in `minimatch@3.1.2` through:
- `@eslint/config-array@0.21.1`
- `@eslint/eslintrc@3.x`
- `eslint` itself

## Approach

Used npm [`overrides`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/configuring-npm/package-json#overrides) to pin vulnerable transitive dependencies to safe versions, rather than running `npm audit fix --force`.

> `npm audit fix --force` would have upgraded `eslint` to v10, which is a breaking change incompatible with `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7.x` (which only supports up to `eslint@^9`).

```json
"overrides": {
  "minimatch": ">=10.2.1",
  "@eslint/config-array": "^0.23.2",
  "@eslint/eslintrc": "^3.3.1"
}

author: jeor
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a simple tool to extract Plex skip-intro / credits marker data and submit it to IntroDB so users can contribute marker timings. 
- Offer a Windows-friendly GUI to choose the Plex DB file and to control behavior (dry run, submission limit, include intro/credits). 
- Keep the tool dependency-free and easy to run by using only the Python standard library (`tkinter`, `sqlite3`, `urllib`).

### Description
- Add `plex_introdb_uploader.py`, a standalone Python GUI that lets users browse for a Plex `com.plexapp.plugins.library.db` file and configure the IntroDB `base_url`, `endpoint`, and Bearer token. 
- Implement marker extraction via a SQLite query on `taggings`/`tags`/`metadata_items` and heuristics via `infer_marker_type`, `infer_offsets`, and `first_int_field` to build `Marker` payloads. 
- Implement submission logic with `post_submission` using `urllib.request`, dry-run logging, optional submission limits, and a small threaded worker that updates an in-app log and status; user settings persist to `~/.plex_introdb_uploader.json`. 
- Add `README.md` with usage notes, typical Windows DB path, and guidance to run in dry-run first.

### Testing
- Running `python -m py_compile plex_introdb_uploader.py` succeeded and validated the script is syntactically correct. 
- An earlier accidental invocation `python -m py_compile plex_introdb_uploader.py README.md` failed because `py_compile` attempted to compile `README.md` as Python and raised a `SyntaxError`. 
- A network check `curl https://api.introdb.app/openapi.json` returned an HTTP 403 in this environment so no live API submission tests were performed here.

author: copilot
body:
The data collector was only runnable as a long-lived HTTP server inside Docker Compose. This replaces that with automated daily collection via GitHub Actions, storing output in a dedicated `data` branch — inspired by the [heissepreise](https://github.com/badlogic/heissepreise) approach.

## Changes

### `data-collector/collect.js` (new)
One-shot script extracted from `index.js`: fetches all stores in parallel, merges price history from a previously stored file, writes `data/latest-canonical.json`, and exits. Output path is overridable via `DATA_FILE` env var.

### `.github/workflows/collect-data.yml` (new)
- Triggers on `schedule` (daily 06:00 UTC) and `workflow_dispatch`
- Fetches previous `data/latest-canonical.json` from the `data` branch before running, enabling cumulative price history
- Runs `npm run collect` with `DATA_FILE` pointed at the workspace root
- Commits and pushes the result to the `data` branch using `git add -f` (bypasses the `data/` `.gitignore` entry intentionally; data never lands on `main`)

### `data-collector/package.json`
Added `"collect": "node collect.js"` script.

### `README.md`
Documents the `main` → `data` branch architecture and manual trigger instructions.

author: samlaycock
body:
## Summary
Adds support for dynamic `import()` expressions in the interpreter when modules are enabled.

Closes #80.

## What changed
- Added parser support for `ImportExpression` in `/src/ast.ts`.
  - `import(` is now parsed as an expression, while `import ... from` remains a declaration.
- Added interpreter runtime support for `import()` in `/src/interpreter.ts`.
  - Added `DynamicImport` language feature flag.
  - Added async `ImportExpression` evaluation path.
  - Dynamic imports now resolve via the existing module resolver/cache code path (`resolveModuleExports`) and return a Promise-like namespace object.
  - Dynamic imports in sync `evaluate()` now raise a clear error directing callers to `evaluateAsync()`.
- Updated ES preset feature coverage in `/src/presets.ts`.
  - ES2020+ now include `DynamicImport` in whitelist presets.
- Updated module docs in `/docs/MODULES.md`.
  - Replaced outdated “No dynamic import()” limitation with async usage guidance.
- Added regression tests:
  - Parser coverage for `import()` in `/test/ast.test.ts`.
  - Module system coverage in `/test/modules.test.ts` for:
    - module context success
    - async script context success
    - authorization failure
    - cache reuse behavior
    - max depth enforcement
- Added changeset: `/.changeset/slow-pumas-reflect.md`.

## Why this approach
The implementation routes dynamic imports through the same resolver/cache/depth enforcement path as static imports to keep behavior and security policy consistent.

## Validation
- `bun run fmt`
- `bun run lint:fix`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test`

body: ### Summary Fixes #277 This PR adds documentation and inline comments clarifying the runtime behavior of Commander's negated flags (`--no-*`). ### Problem There was no explicit documentation regarding the specific contract Commander.js enforces for negated flags (setting the positive key to `false` rather than creating a `no*` key), which is critical for correct option handling by developers and agents. ### Solution Added sections to `AGENTS.md` and `docs/skill/SKILL.md` detailing the contract and added comments to command definitions where these flags are used. ### Key Changes - Updated `AGENTS.md` with a specific contract table for `--no-*` options. - Updated `docs/skill/SKILL.md` with guidelines for automation regarding negated flags. - Added inline comments in `src/commands/new.ts`, `src/commands/schema/migrate.ts`, and `src/commands/search.ts` noting that negated flags map to `false` values on the positive key. ---    --- To clone this PR locally use the [Github CLI](https://cli.github.com/) with command `gh pr checkout 485` You can tag me at @builderio for anything you want me to fix or change

body:
### Motivation
- Garantir que la valeur `step` incrémentée par `exec` (lorsque status passe en `*_done`) remonte correctement dans la chaîne FSM afin d'éviter désynchronisations entre `exec`, `opener`, `gest` et `follower`.
- Assurer que les transitions `open` et `pyramide` sont traitées symétriquement et que le `step` final est disponible pour les composants en aval lors des passages en `*_done` ou `follow`.

### Description
- `project/scripts/opener_from_exec.py` : ingestion étendue pour `exec_type IN ('open','pyramide')`, mapping des statuts (`open_stdby->open_done`, `pyramide_stdby->pyramide_done`) et mise à jour de `opener.step` avec la valeur post-exécution (`exec.step`) tout en matchant la ligne d’origine via `step_done = exec.step - 1`.
- `project/scripts/gest_from_opener.py` : lecture de `step` depuis `opener` et écriture dans `gest` lors des transitions `open_req -> open_done` et `pyramide_req -> pyramide_done`.
- `project/scripts/gest.py` : `ingest_opener_done()` et `mirror_follower_follow()` mis à jour pour copier `step` via `COALESCE(?, step)` afin de propager le `step` depuis `opener` et `follower` lors des transitions `*_done` et `follow`.
- `project/scripts/gest_from_follower_follow.py` : propagation du `step` lors du passage à `follow` en lisant `step` depuis `follower` et en l’insérant dans `gest`.

### Testing
- `python -m py_compile project/scripts/opener_from_exec.py project/scripts/gest_from_opener.py project/scripts/gest_from_follower_follow.py project/scripts/gest.py` was executed and completed without errors.

author: kodex-agent
body:
## Что сделано

По Issue #100 подготовлен архитектурный design-пакет для режима **multi-repo** (только markdown-изменения):

- Добавлен подробный документ с разбором кейсов и целевой моделью:
  - `docs/architecture/multi_repo_mode_design.md`
- Добавлен ADR с фиксацией выбранного варианта и компромиссов:
  - `docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0007-multi-repo-composition-and-docs-federation.md`
- Синхронизированы связанные архитектурные контракты:
  - `docs/architecture/data_model.md`
  - `docs/architecture/api_contract.md`
  - `docs/architecture/prompt_templates_policy.md`
- Обновлена delivery-трассируемость:
  - `docs/delivery/requirements_traceability.md`
  - `docs/delivery/issue_map.md`

## Какие кейсы покрыты

Документирует и поддерживает все целевые режимы из задачи:

1. Монорепо с одним `services.yaml`.
2. Multi-repo, где у каждого repo свой `services.yaml`.
3. Гибрид: центральный orchestrator repo + service repos.
4. Docs в отдельном docs repo.
5. Docs в service repos.
6. Комбинированный docs-режим.

## Выбранный вариант (best option)

Зафиксирован вариант **federated composition**:

- на каждый запуск формируется один `effective services.yaml`;
- источники compose/docs могут быть распределены по нескольким repo;
- резолв выполняется в `control-plane`, исполнение — в `worker`.

Почему выбран:

- закрывает одновременно monorepo/per-repo/hybrid;
- сохраняет архитектурные границы (`external` thin-edge, доменная оркестрация в `internal`, reconcile в `jobs`);
- обеспечивает детерминизм и аудитируемость runtime-решений.

## Trade-offs

Плюсы:

- единая модель для всех project topologies;
- предсказуемый deploy-пайплайн для dev-slot/full-env;
- управляемый role-aware docs context из нескольких repo.

Компромиссы:

- выше сложность resolver/validation;
- нужны расширения metadata repositories и staff API (design backlog);
- увеличится нагрузка на GitHub API в resolve path.

## Влияние на runtime и миграцию

В design-доках зафиксированы:

- целевой runtime алгоритм resolve/compose/deploy;
- расширения data model (`repositories` + composition/docs sources контур);
- planned staff API для composition preview и docs sources;
- phased rollout (`preview -> enforced`) и feature-flag стратегия;
- observability события и метрики для multi-repo режима.

## Проверки

- Scope запуска соблюдён: изменены только `*.md`.
- Выполнен self-check по `docs/design-guidelines/common/check_list.md` (релевантные пункты для doc-only изменения).
- Проверен diff на whitespace-проблемы (`git diff --check`) — ошибок нет.

## Дополнительно

Для валидации технических решений использован Context7 по актуальной документации:

- `github.com/google/go-github/v82` (файлы по `path+ref`, git trees, rate limit handling);
- `k8s.io/client-go` (informer/workqueue/retry/QPS-Burst паттерны).

### Motivation
- Prepare the project to use the OpenCV Android SDK by adding it as a Gradle module and enabling an NDK/CMake native pipeline for future stereo processing work.  
- Provide a minimal, safe native bridge that links OpenCV when present and exposes a simple JNI function to verify the pipeline without changing app behavior.  

### Description
- Included `:opencv` in `settings.gradle.kts` and pointed it at `third_party/opencv-android-sdk/sdk/java` so the SDK can be imported as a module when unzipped.  
- Updated `app/build.gradle.kts` to add `ndkVersion`, `externalNativeBuild` (CMake), a `packaging` rule to pick-first `libc++_shared.so`, and `implementation(project(":opencv"))`.  
- Added native scaffolding: created `app/src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` (CMake >= 3.22, C++17, conditional OpenCV detection and linking) and `app/src/main/cpp/native-lib.cpp` (JNI `openCvVersion()` that returns `cv::getVersionString()` when OpenCV is available, otherwise returns a clear fallback string and logs a warning).  
- Added Kotlin JNI bridge `app/src/main/java/com/pasindu/woundcarepro/native/NativeBridge.kt` that loads `wound_native`.  
- Added a non-fatal smoke-test call to the new bridge in `MainActivity.onCreate()` that logs the OpenCV version or logs an error if loading fails.  
- Added `docs/opencv_android_sdk_setup.md` with instructions to download/unzip the OpenCV Android SDK into `third_party/opencv-android-sdk/`.  
- Added minimal placeholder Gradle module files under `third_party/opencv-android-sdk/sdk/java` so Gradle wiring exists before the official SDK is unpacked (the real SDK should replace this folder).

body:
New module core/httpsManager.js centralizes all HTTP/HTTPS server logic previously inline in index.js (START/END HTTP/HTTPS SERVER SETUP block).

New features:
  - Startup cert analysis: logs subject, issuer, expiry date via X509Certificate Two configurable thresholds: expiryWarningDays (⚠ 60d) + expiryCriticalDays (🔴 15d) Detects self-signed certs, handles corrupted/missing cert gracefully
  - Hot reload: fs.watch() on cert files → setSecureContext() with configurable debounce (debounceMs: 2000) to handle partial writes during certbot renew Logs new expiry date after successful reload
  - ACME HTTP-01 challenge endpoint: GET /.well-known/acme-challenge/:token Registered in Koa router (priority over koa-classic-server) Also patched into HTTP redirect mini-server (AutoRedirect: true case) Auto-creates webroot/.well-known/acme-challenge/ dir with warning if missing Path traversal protection via path.basename() Compatible with: certbot certonly --webroot -w {webroot} -d example.com

  acmeChallenge blocks to https section

author: ibochkarev
body:
### What does it do?
Updates `addSessionContext()` in `modUser` so that `lastlogin` and `thislogin` are only set when adding the **first** session context for the current login (i.e. when `sessionContexts` is empty). `failedlogincount`, `logincount`, and `save()` still run on every new context as before.

### Why is it needed?
When a user had multiple manager contexts and logged into a second one, `lastlogin` and `thislogin` were updated again. That made "Last Login" show the previous session instead of the one before it. By updating these fields only on the first context per login, "Last Login" correctly reflects the prior session.

### How to test
1. Log in to the manager (first context) and note "Last Login" / "This Login".
2. Log in to another manager context (or trigger `addSessionContext` again in the same session).
3. Confirm "Last Login" still shows the previous session and "This Login" the current one, without being overwritten by the second context.

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)
Resolves #16817

author: ishaan-jaff
body:
## Relevant issues

Fixes regression from #21706.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/litellm) directory
- [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

`#21706` narrowed `is_database_connection_error` so only `PrismaError`s with specific connectivity keywords count as connection errors. That was the right intent for the reconnect logic, but it also silently changed the `allow_requests_on_db_unavailable` behavior as a side effect — requests now only get let through on real transport errors, not on any prisma error.

The root cause: one method was serving two purposes with different semantics.

**Fix:**
- Add `is_database_transport_error` — narrow, keyword-gated check for cases where a reconnect actually makes sense (DB is unreachable, connection dropped). Data-layer errors like `UniqueViolationError` mean the DB IS up, so reconnecting is pointless.
- Restore `is_database_connection_error` to its original broad behavior (any `PrismaError` subclass) for the `allow_requests_on_db_unavailable` path.
- Update the two reconnect call sites from #21706 (`auth_checks.py` key lookup retry, `utils.py` watchdog) to use `is_database_transport_error`.
- Update the tests from #21706 that asserted the narrow behavior onto `is_database_connection_error` — move those assertions to `is_database_transport_error` where they belong.

**Files changed:**
- `litellm/proxy/db/exception_handler.py` — add `is_database_transport_error`, restore `is_database_connection_error`
- `litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py` — reconnect retry uses `is_database_transport_error`
- `litellm/proxy/utils.py` — watchdog uses `is_database_transport_error`
- `tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_exception_handler.py` — assert narrow behavior on `is_database_transport_error`
- `tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_prisma_self_heal.py` — patch `is_database_transport_error` in watchdog test

body:
### Motivation
- Improve routing decisions for multi-turn conversations by surfacing recent session context to the router so follow-ups don't lose intent.
- Strengthen fast-path signals beyond naive length/keyword checks to better detect complex or external-context requests that should go to cloud providers (`Ego`).
- Harden session-history ingestion to avoid placeholder/empty messages and duplicate latest-user injection that corrupt prompt construction.

### Description
- Enhanced `fast_path_classify` in `crates/abigail-router/src/router.rs` to use a richer `calculate_id_instinct` that combines length bands, complexity keyword scoring, structured-content detection, and multi-question boosts, and added `has_external_context_signal` to detect web/API/docs cues.
- Adjusted Ego-feasibility and target thresholds so external-context signals can route to `Ego` while keeping short/local prompts on `Id` and added two regression tests for these behaviors in the router test module (`test_fast_path_classify_prefers_ego_for_external_context` and `test_fast_path_classify_keeps_short_local_message_on_id`).
- Hardened session history handling in `tauri-app/src/commands/chat.rs` by adding `SessionMessage`, `sanitize_session_history`, and `build_contextual_messages` to trim/limit history, drop non-user/assistant or empty entries, truncate long messages, and avoid duplicating the latest user turn.
- Updated `chat` and `chat_stream` to accept optional `session_messages` and to build requests via `build_contextual_messages`, and updated the UI `tauri-app/src-ui/src/components/ChatInterface.tsx` to send a stable `sessionBeforeTurn` snapshot (excluding empty placeholders) when invoking `chat_stream`.
- Fixed a malformed newline literal bug in the router and tuned thresholds so the new tests pass reliably.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo test -p abigail-router --lib`, which executed the router unit test suite and related tests; all tests passed (`118 passed; 0 failed`).
- Ran the frontend unit tests with `npm test -- ChatInterface` in `tauri-app/src-ui`, and the `ChatInterface` tests passed (`1 test file, 3 tests passed`).

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
- **Wrapped native library loading** (`osu.Android.Native`) in a `try-catch` block within `OsuGameActivity.OnCreate`. This prevents the application from crashing immediately if the native library (containing Oboe/Vulkan drivers) fails to load (e.g., `UnsatisfiedLinkError`). The app can now proceed, and specific drivers will gracefully fail later if enabled.
- **Hardened Ruleset Loading**: Replaced string-based `Assembly.Load("...")` with `Assembly.Load(typeof(...).Assembly.FullName)` wrapped in `try-catch`.
    -   **Linker Safety**: Using `typeof()` creates a strong static reference to the ruleset types (`OsuRuleset`, `TaikoRuleset`, etc.), ensuring the Xamarin/Android linker does not strip these assemblies in Release builds. This is a common cause of "crash on startup" in deployed APKs.
    -   **Error Handling**: Added logging to capture and non-fatally handle any issues during ruleset preloading.
- **Added Defensive Null Checks**: Inserted runtime null checks for `Window`, `WindowManager`, and `Resources` in `OnCreate` before accessing their properties, replacing `Debug.Assert` which is removed in Release builds.
- **Async Safety**: Wrapped the `handleImportFromUris` async task body in a `try-catch` block to prevent unobserved task exceptions from crashing the process.

These changes collectively address the reported "crash on open" issue on the S23 Ultra by handling the most likely causes: stripped assemblies and native library loading failures.

body:
When working with C⋆-algebras, it is common to consider alternate topologies (e.g., the strict topology on the multiplier algebra, or the ultraweak, ultrastrong, ultrastrong-⋆ or Mackey topologies associated to a W⋆-algebra via its predual). In Mathlib, this is done via type synonyms.

The `ContinuousFunctoinalCalculus` class was semi-recently refactored to make it possible (by not assuming that `cfcHom` is a closed embedding, only that it is continuous and injective) to allow for instances on these type synonyms.

This PR creates the basic framework for transferring these instances from the C⋆-algebra to its type synonyms. Note that C⋆-norm topology is pretty much the strongest topology one ever considers in the context of C⋆-algebras, so it is not at all problematic that we can't transfer to type synonyms with a stronger topology.

## Summary

- **Python ServiceExtractor** (LangGraph node): async LLM extraction pipeline using Gemini via LangChain. Filters `.go`/`.py` files, batches by token budget, extracts `ServiceNode` and `CallsEdge` Pydantic models with structured output, deduplicates, and handles rate limits via tenacity retry + asyncio semaphore.

## Summary

Implements the event-driven historical replay engine (`src/sysls/backtest/replay.py`) for Phase 4 backtesting:

- **ReplayEngine** creates a sandboxed environment (SimulatedClock, EventBus, OMS, PaperVenue) and feeds historical data through the full live stack for realistic simulation
- Strategies receive events through the standard `on_market_data` lifecycle, identical to live execution

- `sysls.strategy.base.Strategy`, `StrategyContext` — strategy lifecycle

author: coreyn
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a comprehensive environmental noise filtering stage as the first step in the audio processing pipeline. The change addresses real-world recording conditions where background noise (appliances, traffic, etc.) can degrade downstream processing accuracy.

## Key Changes

- **New pipeline stage:** Added environmental noise filtering as step 1, shifting all subsequent stages down by one position (source separation becomes step 2, metronome analysis becomes step 3, etc.)

- **Hybrid filtering approach:** Designed a three-layer noise filtering strategy:
  - Layer 1: Spectral gating for stationary noise (appliance hum, HVAC rumble)
  - Layer 2: Adaptive notch filtering for tonal interference (50/60 Hz mains hum, motor tones)
  - Layer 3: ML denoiser (RNNoise-style or lightweight Conv-TasNet) for non-stationary noise (sirens, engines, transients)

- **Detailed noise taxonomy:** Added comprehensive documentation of noise categories (appliance hum, motor noise, sirens, impacts, ambient broadband) with their spectral and temporal characteristics

- **Noise profile estimation:** Integrated noise calibration into the existing "listening for tempo..." phase, with continuous updates during detected rest periods

- **ML denoiser specifications:** Defined architecture requirements (RNNoise-style GRU ~60K parameters or small U-Net), input/output formats, and graceful degradation for high-noise environments

- **Training data strategy:** Expanded synthetic data generation to include 10,000+ noise filtering clips with diverse environmental noise sources (appliances, vehicles, street noise, household sounds, weather, construction)

- **Updated project structure:** Added new files to support noise filtering:
  - `audio/noise_filter.py` - Environmental noise filtering implementation
  - `models/noise_model.py` - PyTorch noise filtering model
  - `training/noise_sources.py` - Noise dataset curation
  - `training/train_noise_filter.py` - Model training script

- **Latency budgeting:** Added explicit latency allocation for noise filtering (2–5ms) in the real-time feedback requirements

- **Phase 1 roadmap update:** Added basic spectral gating as an early PoC step before custom ML denoiser

- **Validation strategy:** Included guidance for testing noise filter robustness with real recordings of intentional background noise

## Implementation Details

The noise filtering stage operates before source separation to prevent environmental noise from corrupting metronome click detection and onset detection. The hybrid approach balances computational efficiency (spectral gating and notch filtering are near-instant) with robustness (ML denoiser handles complex, non-stationary noise). The denoiser is intentionally kept lightweight (<5ms inference) to fit within the real-time latency budget, and the system includes SNR estimation to warn users when environmental conditions are too noisy for reliable analysis.

This pull request standardizes the naming of the SCORM content path setting for improved clarity and consistency. The setting previously known as `WAGTAIL_LMS_CONTENT_PATH` has been renamed to `WAGTAIL_LMS_SCORM_CONTENT_PATH`, with the old name deprecated but still supported for backward compatibility (a warning will be issued if used). All references throughout the codebase, documentation, and tests have been updated to use the new name.

**Deprecation and Backward Compatibility:**
- The `WAGTAIL_LMS_CONTENT_PATH` setting is now deprecated in favor of `WAGTAIL_LMS_SCORM_CONTENT_PATH`. Using the old name emits a `DeprecationWarning`, but its value is still honored for backward compatibility. The old name is still accessible in `conf.py` for downstream code. author: orxfun
body:
Introduces the **experiment** feature to enable experimenting algorithmic ideas. Also introduces parallel merging of sorted arrays as first of these experiments.

The experimental implementation of the algorithm practices the dual safety documentation:

* unsafe methods provide a numbered list of requirements that need to be satisfied to be able to safely call the method,
* the caller explains how it satisfies each of these conditions.

In addition to "criterion", [orx-criterion](https://github.com/orxfun/orx-criterion) is utilized to enable parameter tuning. The idea is to add interesting parameters to the algorithm, carry out extensive experiments and tune the parameters. Eventually, the best performing variant enters the library without the "experiment" feature.
