author: ehesp
body:
While Genkit currently supports Express, the modern JavaScript ecosystem is rapidly consolidating around Web Standard APIs (Request, Response, Headers). This PR introduces a new plugin that allows Genkit flows to be exposed via the Fetch API standard, making Genkit natively compatible with virtually every modern JS runtime and framework.

By moving away from Node-specific HTTP abstractions, Genkit can now run seamlessly at the Edge, in Serverless environments, and in high-performance runtimes like Bun and Deno:

Runtimes:

- Bun
- Deno
- Cloudflare Workers (Workerd)
- Node (18+) via fetch
- Edge (Vercel, Netlify, Fastly)
- ... and probably more

Frameworks:

- Hono
- Elysia
- Astro
- Remix
- Nitro (+ frameworks built on-top of it)
- TanStack Start
- ... and probably more

 Usage (e.g. Hono):
 
```ts
const app = new Hono();

// Mount a single flow
app.all('/myFlow', (c) => handleFlow(c.req.raw, myFlow));

// Mount Genkit flows under /api - handleFlows routes by path
app.all('/api/*', (c) => handleFlows(c.req.raw, flows, '/api'));
```

This PR also includes a sample `js-hono`.

author: scotwells
body:
## Summary
- Add environment variables for NATS TLS configuration to processor deployment
- Add KUBECONFIG env var to controller-manager deployment
- Enables overlays to configure TLS by patching env vars instead of rewriting args

## Changes

**Processor** (`config/base/processor.yaml`):
- `NATS_TLS_ENABLED` (default: false)
- `NATS_TLS_CERT_FILE`
- `NATS_TLS_KEY_FILE`
- `NATS_TLS_CA_FILE`
- `HEALTH_PROBE_ADDR` (default: :8081)

**Controller-manager** (`config/base/controller-manager.yaml`):
- `KUBECONFIG` (default: empty, uses in-cluster config)

## Why
Environment-specific overlays (like staging) previously had to rewrite the entire args list to add TLS flags. This caused maintenance issues when flags changed in the code. Now overlays only need to patch env var values and add volume mounts.

author: seanwevans
body:
### Motivation
- Replace abrupt process termination on CUDA failures with exception propagation so callers can handle errors while preserving `cudaGetErrorString` diagnostics.
- Make CUDA and Raylib resource allocation and teardown exception-safe so partial initialization cannot leak device or host resources.
- Ensure all allocation paths have deterministic release semantics on both error and normal exit.

### Description
- Changed `ck`/`CK` to throw `std::runtime_error` including `cudaGetErrorString(...)` instead of calling `exit(1)` so CUDA diagnostics are preserved in propagated errors.
- Made `alloc_Us` and `alloc_Cs` initialize pointers to `nullptr` and free any partially-allocated device memory on allocation failures before rethrowing.
- Added small RAII helpers: `CudaBuffer<T>` (owns a device pointer), `DeviceUsoa`/`DeviceCsoa` (wrap SoA device allocations), `HostPixels` (owns `malloc`/`free` host buffer), and `RaylibWindowGuard`/`RaylibTextureGuard` (wrap `InitWindow`/`CloseWindow` and `LoadTextureFromImage`/`UnloadTexture`).
- Rewrote `main` to use the RAII wrappers and a `try`/`catch` boundary so normal and error exits deterministically release resources; existing cleanup operations (`cudaFree`, `free_Us`/`free_Cs`, `UnloadTexture`, `CloseWindow`, `free`) are preserved by destructors.

### Testing
- Attempted an automated compile-check with `nvcc -std=c++17 -c tau_hypersonic_cuda.cu -o /tmp/tau.o`, which failed because `nvcc` is not available in the execution environment (`bash: command not found: nvcc`).

author: setchy
body:
## Summary

Completes the renderer state-management migration started with the filters store (#2633): **TanStack Query owns all API state, Zustand stores own all client state, and `AppContext` is gone.**

- **TanStack Query** owns notification fetching, polling (`refetchInterval`), caching, retries, and mutations (mark as read/done, unsubscribe), replacing the manual `useState`/timer-based fetching in `useNotifications`.
- **Zustand stores** own accounts (`useAccountsStore`) and settings (`useSettingsStore`) state, joining the existing filters store. Both persist to their own local storage keys, with a one-time migration from the legacy `gitify-storage` key.
- **`AppContext` is fully retired.** Components consume focused hooks directly: `useNotifications()` (shared query cache), `useLogins()` (forge login/logout flows), `useOnlineStatus()`, and a small transient store for global-shortcut registration state. A one-mount `GlobalEffects` component hosts app-level side effects (theme, tray, shortcut registration, app reset, account refresh, notification alerts).

## Details

- **Instant client-side filtering**: the notifications cache holds unfiltered data and all filtering happens in the query `select`, so narrowing *and loosening* filters applies instantly with zero API calls. Enrichment is limited to filter-passing notifications to bound API usage.
- Notification queries are keyed by **account identity** (UUIDs), not account count, so adding/removing/swapping accounts always resolves to distinct cache entries; re-authentication explicitly invalidates.
- Store side effects (auto launch, tray icons, keep-window-on-blur, zoom sync) live in `stores/subscriptions.ts`, initialized once on app startup.
- The accounts store delegates to the existing `utils/auth/utils` logic (multi-forge upsert, scope checks), sanitizes persisted state on rehydrate, and owns token re-encryption migration (run once before the first account refresh).
- Fetch scheduling honours the interval/inactivity `fetchType` setting: interval mode maps to TanStack Query's `refetchInterval`; inactivity mode reuses `useInactivityTimer`.
- Online/offline state flows from TanStack Query's `onlineManager` through the renderer to the tray (`ITrayColorUpdate` IPC payload) instead of polling `net.isOnline()` in the main process, and surfaces an `OFFLINE` error state in the UI.
- `@octokit/plugin-retry` removed; retries are handled at the query layer (queries and mutations). `useIntervalTimer` removed (superseded by query polling).
- Tests: component tests keep the `renderWithProviders` options API, now backed by globally mocked hooks (`__helpers__/hook-mocks.ts`) plus direct store seeding; hook tests exercise the real implementations via `vi.unmock`.

author: titaniumtim
body:
### Motivation
- Reduce transient 502 failures encountered when starting games due to upstream FastF1 / schedule provider outages.
- Serve deterministic session lists while preventing future seasons from being exposed and filtering invalid/duplicate sessions.
- Provide a fallback strategy so the frontend can continue to function during short upstream outages.

### Description
- Added `load_session_with_retry` which retries `fastf1.get_session(...).load(...)` up to `MAX_SESSION_LOAD_ATTEMPTS` with a short delay to mitigate transient errors.
- Implemented two-tier caching for `/session_results` and `/circuit_map` using `fresh` (short TTL) and `stale` (longer TTL) cache keys in `api_cache`, returning stale data on upstream failure when available and preserving a 502 when no fallback exists.
- Made schedule retrieval resilient by wrapping `get_event_schedule` in a cached helper `get_schedule` that stores successful schedules and returns cached schedules when upstream calls fail.
- Kept previous fixes: dynamic `years()` capped to current UTC year and cleaned session enumeration that filters empty/NaN names, skips sessions with missing dates, and de-duplicates based on normalized `(name.lower(), iso_date)` keys.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall main.py` which succeeded and validated syntax.
- Executed a runtime smoke script that verified `years()` returns the current range, seeded stale cache entries, forced loader failures, and confirmed `/session_results` and `/circuit_map` returned the seeded stale values (fallback behavior verified).
- Confirmed 502 behavior still occurs when neither fresh nor stale cache exists by invoking `session_results` for a non-existent upstream year (HTTP 502 verified).

### Motivation
- Allow the hypersonic CUDA simulation to run on arbitrary grid sizes instead of being fixed to 1600x512 while preserving the original default.
- Make device indexing, face counts, buffers and host-side render/texture setup honor runtime dimensions for correctness and flexibility.

### Description
- Added `width` and `height` fields to `SimConfig` with `DEFAULT_WIDTH=1600` and `DEFAULT_HEIGHT=512` to keep previous behavior as the default.
- Parsed new CLI flags `--width` and `--height` (with integer parsing and validation) and adjusted geometry defaults to scale with runtime dimensions unless explicit geometry flags are provided.
- Replaced compile-time `W`/`H` uses with runtime `d_cfg.width`/`d_cfg.height` in device helpers and kernels (including `d_idx()`, boundary clamps, `N`, face counts, indexing math and sampling functions).
- Updated host-side allocations, kernel launch extents, image/texture sizes, and draw rectangles to use `h_cfg.width`/`h_cfg.height` so buffers and launches match runtime dimensions.

body:
The "Link kopieren" button was only writing to the clipboard; the expected behaviour is to open the native Share Sheet (Web Share API).

## Changes

- **`RecipeDetail.js`** — `handleCopyShareUrl` now calls `navigator.share()` first. `AbortError` (user dismisses the sheet) is swallowed; any other error falls through to the existing clipboard path. Browsers without Web Share API continue to use clipboard copy unchanged.

```js
if (navigator.share) {
  try {
    await navigator.share({ url, title: recipe.title });
    return;
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name === 'AbortError') return;
    // fall through to clipboard
  }
}
```

- **`RecipeDetail.test.js`** — two new tests covering the `navigator.share` path and the clipboard fallback when `navigator.share` is absent.

author: ecto
body:
## Description

Add support for the [Loon](https://github.com/ecto/loon) programming language — a functional language with invisible types, safe ownership, and algebraic effects.

Loon uses square brackets `[...]` as its primary expression delimiter (similar to a Lisp), with unique syntax for algebraic effects, pattern matching, algebraic data types, and pipe-based functional composition.

### Changes

- **TextMate grammar** (`source.loon`) with highlighting for:
  - Special forms (`fn`, `let`, `match`, `pipe`, `handle`, `type`, `test`, etc.)
  - Function definitions and calls
  - Type constructors (capitalized identifiers)
  - Module access (`IO.read-file`, `math.add`)
  - Effect sets (`#{IO Fail}`)
  - Keywords (`:desc`, `:as`)
  - Vectors (`#[1 2 3]`), maps (`{}`), tuples (`()`)
  - Strings with interpolation, numbers, comments (`;`)
- **Language entry** in `languages.yml` with `.oo` (primary) and `.loon` extensions
- **Four samples** from the real codebase: word counting, algebraic types, effect handling, and performance profiling

### Example

```
[type Shape
  [Circle f64]
  [Rect f64 f64]
  Point]

[fn area [shape]
  [match shape
    [Circle r] [* 3.14159 [* r r]]
    [Rect w h] [* w h]
    Point      0.0]]
```

### Search results

https://github.com/search?q=path%3A*.oo+%5Bfn+&type=code

### License

The grammar is MIT licensed. Samples are written by the repo author and included under MIT.

author: jasoncarreira
body:
## Overview

Add optional Phoenix/OpenTelemetry tracing integration to provide visibility into agent operations.

Closes #344

## Features

- **Optional dependencies**: Phoenix packages in `optionalDependencies`, no hard requirement
- **Zero overhead when disabled**: No tracing overhead if env vars not set
- **Graceful degradation**: Works fine without Phoenix packages installed
- **OpenInference conventions**: Follows industry standard semantic conventions

## What's Traced

- Input/output for each agent turn
- Reasoning accumulation (batched for efficiency)
- Tool calls with parameters
- Tool results (with size limits)
- Token counts and costs
- Errors and exceptions

## Configuration

### Environment Variables
```bash
# Enable tracing (local Phoenix)
PHOENIX_COLLECTOR_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:6006

# Or use Phoenix cloud
PHOENIX_API_KEY=your-api-key

# Project name (default: lettabot)
PHOENIX_PROJECT_NAME=lettabot
```

## Implementation Details

### New Module: `src/tracing/index.ts`
- Clean API with `initTracing()` and `traceAgentTurn()`
- Lazy loading of Phoenix packages
- No-op pattern for zero overhead when disabled
- Type-safe TracingSpan interface

### Integration Points
- `src/main.ts`: Initialize tracing before other imports
- `src/core/bot.ts`: Wrap agent turns in trace spans

### Dependencies Added (optional)
- `@arizeai/phoenix-otel@^0.4.1`
- `@arizeai/openinference-core@^2.0.5`

## Testing

✅ Works normally without Phoenix installed
✅ Zero overhead when disabled
✅ Comprehensive tracing when enabled

## Documentation

- Updated `.env.example` with Phoenix configuration
- Inline code documentation
- Usage examples in module header

## Benefits

- **Visibility**: See exactly what the agent is doing
- **Debugging**: Track tool calls and reasoning
- **Cost tracking**: Monitor LLM costs per conversation
- **Performance**: Identify slow operations
- **Production ready**: Optional, zero overhead, graceful fallbacks

### Motivation
- Shift combat toward more tactical, reactive play by giving enemies intent and simple AI profiles, adding conditional/combination rewards for deliberate play, and a defensive option to encourage reactive turns. 
- Preserve existing save compatibility and keep changes minimal and localized to the combat/runtime surface so no migration is required. 

### Description
- Added lightweight tactical runtime fields and safe defaults (`lastPlayerSkill`, `lastPlayerTags`, `comboWindow`, `avoidedDamageLastTurn`) and normalized them in `ensureStateIntegrity()` to avoid breaking saves. 
- Implemented reactive enemy AI via `chooseEnemyIntent()` plus AI profiles (`Aggressive`, `Defensive`, `Opportunist`), displayed in the enemy panel as an intent label, and seeded per-encounter in `startCombat()`. 
- Introduced conditional/combination systems: `tacticalSkillBonus()` applies moderate bonuses for debuffed targets, HP windows, avoided-damage momentum, and combo triggers detected by `comboTriggerFor()` using a 3-turn combo window; activations are logged. 
- Implemented boss reaction tracking in `trackBossReaction()` to increase temporary resistance after repeated same-tag skill usage and reset on phase change, and added stack visibility + diminishing returns (cap 5, potency scaled after threshold) for statuses. 
- Added a defensive action `Brace` that grants short mitigation and small resource recovery, and made skill cooldowns transparent by showing effective CD (with CDR) on skill buttons and tooltip details. 
- Integrated systems into combat flow: player actions record last skill/tags and update combo window, `applySkill()` multiplies damage by tactical bonus and calls boss reaction tracking, and `enemyTurn()` logs intent and executes buff/debuff/attack branches without exposing numbers. 

### Testing

- `node --check sw.js` — succeeded. 
- Served locally with `python -m http.server 8116` and ran a Playwright smoke interaction that exercised Hunt → active combat UI, used the `Brace` action, inspected skill button cooldown labeling, and produced a screenshot (`artifacts/batch4-tactical-upgrade.png`), which completed successfully after an initial selector ambiguity in the test harness.

author: copilot
body:
Some crawlers use internal/API URLs as their deduplication key (e.g. ArcGIS REST endpoints for sofiyska-voda, single-page incident lists for toplo-bg and erm-zapad), which were being surfaced verbatim as user-facing deeplinks. Valid links (WordPress post permalinks) also had no visual indicator.

## Changes

**Decouple user-facing URL from deduplication URL**
- Added `deepLinkUrl?: string` to `SourceDocumentWithGeoJson` — empty string explicitly disables the link; omitting it falls back to `url` (backward-compatible for WordPress crawlers)
- Added `sourceDocumentId?: string` to `MessageIngestOptions` — when provided, used directly instead of deriving from `sourceUrl`, ensuring deduplication always stays tied to `source.url` regardless of what `sourceUrl` carries
- `from-sources.ts` now passes `sourceDocumentId` from `source.url` and `sourceUrl` from the resolved user-facing URL separately

**Disable deeplinks for crawlers without user-facing pages**
- `toplo-bg`, `sofiyska-voda`, `erm-zapad`: `deepLinkUrl: ""`

**Frontend: make valid links visually obvious**
- `Source.tsx` adds underline + external-link icon (↗) when `sourceUrl` is a valid `https://` URL; plain text otherwise

```typescript
// sourceDocumentId always from source.url (deduplication)
// sourceUrl carries user-facing URL from deepLinkUrl if set
const userFacingUrl =
  source.deepLinkUrl !== undefined
    ? source.deepLinkUrl || undefined   // "" → no link
    : source.url;

await messageIngest(source.message, source.sourceType, {
  sourceUrl: userFacingUrl,
  sourceDocumentId,   // derived from source.url, never from deepLinkUrl
  ...
});
```

author: unbelievableflavour
body:
This Pr includes a game-specific fixes system which is useable by all game sources. For now it fixes Fallout 3,4, and new vegas, but allows for many more.

Fallout games are just registry keys added. But this system also allows for adding DLL files for instance:
Example of that:
```
package app.gamenative.gamefixes

/**
 * Example DLL inclusion fix. Place DLL at: context.filesDir/gamefixes_dlls/redist/MyFix.dll
 * Add (GameSource.GOG to "0") to GameFixesRegistry.fixes to enable.
 */
val GOG_Fix_0: GameFix = DllInclusionFix(
    dllRelativePath = "redist/MyFix.dll",
    targetSubdir = "",
)
```

```
package app.gamenative.gamefixes

import android.content.Context
import timber.log.Timber
import java.io.File

/**
 * Copies a DLL from a source path into the game install directory.
 * Source is relative to [dllBaseDir] (e.g. context.filesDir / "gamefixes_dlls").
 * [targetSubdir] is a subdir under install path (e.g. "" for game root, "subfolder" for installPath/subfolder).
 */
class DllInclusionFix(
    private val dllRelativePath: String,
    private val targetSubdir: String = "",
    private val dllBaseDir: (Context) -> File = { ctx -> File(ctx.filesDir, "gamefixes_dlls") },
) : GameFix {
    override fun apply(
        context: Context,
        gameId: String,
        installPath: String,
        installPathWindows: String,
    ): Boolean {
        val baseDir = dllBaseDir(context)
        val sourceFile = File(baseDir, dllRelativePath)
        if (!sourceFile.isFile) {
            Timber.tag("GameFixes").w("DLL not found: ${sourceFile.absolutePath}")
            return false
        }
        val targetDir = if (targetSubdir.isEmpty()) File(installPath) else File(installPath, targetSubdir)
        targetDir.mkdirs()
        val targetFile = File(targetDir, sourceFile.name)
        return try {
            sourceFile.copyTo(targetFile, overwrite = true)
            Timber.tag("GameFixes").d("Copied ${sourceFile.name} to game dir for game $gameId")
            true
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            Timber.tag("GameFixes").e(e, "Failed to copy DLL for game $gameId")
            false
        }
    }
}
```

body: Long lines of Torah/Tanach text were not wrapping at all — every word rendered on a single overflowing line. The previous attempt to fix mid-word breaks left `white-space: pre-wrap` in place, which combined with no actual whitespace between `` elements meant zero soft-wrap opportunities existed. ## Root cause Each word is rendered as an adjacent `` with no text node between them. `word-spacing` adds visual gaps but not wrap points. Without space characters, the browser has nowhere to break lines regardless of `white-space` or `word-break` settings. ## Changes - **`TextDisplay.tsx`** — Wrap each word `` in `React.Fragment` (keyed) and emit `{' '}` after it, inserting a real space character between every word: ```tsx {displayText} {' '} ``` - **`App.module.css`** — Change `white-space: pre-wrap` → `white-space: normal`; `pre-wrap` is inappropriate for dynamically-rendered inline content and was a leftover from the previous fix attempt. ## Result ![Text wrapping screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a06933c-4300-476e-ac03-79025aeb9113) Lines wrap at word boundaries; no mid-word breaks. --- 💡 You can make Copilot smarter by setting up custom instructions, customizing its development environment and configuring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. **Changes:**
- Restructured the section to distinguish between push (outbound) and fetch (inbound) operations
- Added documentation for the new `_sync_worktree_with_remote()` function that handles orchestrator restart scenarios
- Clarified when each operation runs and what failure modes are handled

**Context:**
The previous documentation only described the push-to-remote behavior (orchestrator writes artifacts, pushes to remote). PR #855 added the complementary fetch-from-remote operation that runs before pipeline phase execution to ensure the local worktree is in sync with commits pushed by agents in previous phases. This prevents `ContractNotFoundError` after orchestrator restarts.

author: orbasker
body:
## What changed

- **Realtime types** (`realtime_types.dart`): Added `RealtimeMessage` and `RealtimeService` interface aligned with the backend and Angular realtime contract (message types: `game_update`, `phase_update`, `bid_selection`, `trick_selection`, etc.).
- **WebSocket realtime service** (`websocket_realtime_service.dart`): Implemented `WebSocketRealtimeService` that connects to the same backend endpoint as the web app (`/api/v1/ws/games/{gameId}`), with optional JWT in the query string. Includes reconnect logic (up to 5 attempts, 3s delay) and exposes a stream of parsed messages plus connection status.
- **GameService integration**: `GameService` now takes an optional `RealtimeService`, extends `ChangeNotifier`, and on `loadGame(gameId)` connects to the WebSocket and subscribes to the message stream. Incoming messages update game state, phase, live bid/trick/trump selections, and rounds (e.g. refetch on `tricks_submitted`). Added send methods: `sendSubmitBids`, `sendSubmitTricks`, `sendBidSelection`, `sendTrickSelection`, `sendTrumpSelection`, and the remaining ephemeral types (`sendBetChange`, `sendBetLocked`, `sendRoundResultChanged`, `sendRoundScoreLocked`). Realtime is disconnected on `clearGame()` and when leaving a game (e.g. delete). Added `setAuthToken(String?)` for future auth.
- **App wiring**: In `main.dart`, introduced a shared `_apiBaseUrl`, registered `RealtimeService` (WebSocket implementation) and `ProxyProvider2<ApiService, RealtimeService, GameService>` so `GameService` receives both API and realtime.
- **UI**: Game screen shows a realtime connection indicator in the app bar (filled/outline circle) and displays `realtimeError` when the backend sends an error over the socket.
- **Dependency**: Added `web_socket_channel: ^3.0.0` in `pubspec.yaml`.

## Why

The task was to add a realtime layer to the Whist Flutter app so it uses the same backend WebSocket (or Supabase Realtime) as the web app. This allows the mobile app to receive live game updates (`game_update`, `phase_update`, `bid_selection`, `trick_selection`, etc.) and to send actions (`submit_bids`, `submit_tricks`, `bid_selection`, etc.) over the same channel, keeping game state in sync across clients without polling.

## Implementation details

- **URL derivation**: WS URL is built from the API base URL (e.g. `http://localhost:8000/api/v1` → `ws://localhost:8000/api/v1/ws/games/{gameId}?token=...`), matching the Angular frontend.
- **RealtimeService abstraction**: The interface allows swapping in a Supabase Realtime implementation later if the backend publishes to it; the current PR uses the backend WebSocket only.
- **GameService as ChangeNotifier**: So that when realtime messages update `_gameState`, `_rounds`, or live selections, `notifyListeners()` is called and the existing `Consumer<GameService>` UI rebuilds.
- **Auth**: Backend requires JWT on the WebSocket. The app currently passes `token: null`; when auth is added, call `gameService.setAuthToken(accessToken)` so the next connect (or reconnect) uses the token.

author: lassestilvang
body:
**What:**
- Added a composite index on `(listId, createdAt)` to the `tasks` table in `src/lib/schema.ts` to optimize queries that filter by `listId` (specifically for the Inbox where `listId` is null) and sort by `createdAt`.
- Fixed broken migration metadata in `drizzle/meta/0007_snapshot.json` and `drizzle/0007_adorable_tempest.sql` to resolve conflicts and enable correct migration generation.
- Generated new migration `0008_tiresome_giant_girl.sql` including the new index and synchronizing other missing indexes.
- Added `scripts/benchmark-inbox-sort.ts` to measure performance improvement.
- Fixed a flaky test in `src/app/api/tasks/route.test.ts` by mocking the cache module.

**Why:**
- Queries filtering by `listId` and sorting by `createdAt` were performing a sort in memory, which is inefficient for large datasets.
- The new index allows the database to retrieve pre-sorted results directly.

**Measured Improvement:**
- Benchmark script: `scripts/benchmark-inbox-sort.ts`

## Summary

- Add `Validate()` methods to `tlsutil.Config` and `tlsutil.ClientConfig` that check file existence with descriptive error messages before TLS setup attempts to read them
- Call `Validate()` automatically from `TLSConfig()` and `HTTPClient()`, so all callers across the codebase benefit without code changes: vault plugin, vault-manager, webui, mirror, marketplace, and CLI plugin commands
- Add 10 tests covering both `Validate()` methods (empty config, valid files, missing cert/key/CA with message assertions)

## Context

When a plugin is configured with a TLS file path that doesn't exist (e.g. `ca_cert: /path/to/ca.crt` placeholder left in `zhi.yaml`), the error surfaces as a generic go-plugin handshake failure:

```
Unrecognized remote plugin message:
Failed to read any lines from plugin's stdout
```

The actual cause (`os.ReadFile` on a nonexistent path) was logged to the plugin's stderr but never reached the user. Now the error is caught early with a clear message like:

```
CA certificate file not found at "/path/to/ca.crt": stat /path/to/ca.crt: no such file or directory
```

author: mikealhayek
body:
This pull request refactors the MCP resource URI handling to use URI templates with named variables, simplifying how resource types declare and match URIs. It replaces the previous pattern-based and strategy-provider approach with a unified template system, updates the handler interfaces and base classes accordingly, and improves documentation and extensibility for custom resource types.

**Core API and Handler Refactoring:**

* The `IMcpResourceTypeHandler` interface and `McpResourceTypeHandlerBase` now use a dictionary of variables extracted from URI templates instead of passing a parsed `McpResourceUri` object, making handler implementations more flexible and template-driven. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-816cc040caa82b8e6a0af829e4ed05efaca763dedbb139a4054ee0afbf55ab2dR21-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7cc21ecc56b0ecfe01519c98623b2e86d7116bfc163416e998d4f6c2188f2ddbL7-R8) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7cc21ecc56b0ecfe01519c98623b2e86d7116bfc163416e998d4f6c2188f2ddbL23-R38)
* The `McpResourceUri` class is now a static utility providing methods for URI template matching and variable extraction (e.g., `TryMatch`), removing the previous object model and centralizing template logic.

**Resource Type Extensibility and Metadata:**

* Resource types now declare their supported variables via the new `McpResourceVariable` type, replacing the old `UriPatterns` property. This metadata is used to inform the UI and consumers about which placeholders are valid for each resource type.
* The `IContentResourceStrategyProvider` interface and related extension points have been removed, as the new template-based system supersedes the need for strategy providers.

**Documentation and Usability Improvements:**

* Documentation has been significantly updated to explain the new URI template system, supported variables, and how to implement custom resource types and handlers. The admin UI and recipes now display and use variable placeholders instead of hardcoded patterns. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a2c02e72d080f8e7e1196a12fb8c986e047ac246c2d374a52fa4c64072a20df4L191-R279) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a2c02e72d080f8e7e1196a12fb8c986e047ac246c2d374a52fa4c64072a20df4L310-R301)

**Module and Handler Updates:**

* The FTP resource type handler and module startup have been updated to use the new variable-based approach, extracting the remote path from the variables dictionary and declaring supported variables for the UI. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fabe81204adbde4ef9ce2818d00bea1ec02a1f5bcfc7a87aa056d49d4b4a1df7L33-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fabe81204adbde4ef9ce2818d00bea1ec02a1f5bcfc7a87aa056d49d4b4a1df7L61-R63) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-15e23f085d45f75ac1f71b3f28686a10819dcdcb71f1f8e30ec62f12e2546bbaL27-R30)

**New Extensibility Interfaces:**

* Added `IMcpFileProviderResolver` for resolving file providers by name, supporting more flexible file resource patterns.

body:
Bootstraps a repository structure for containerised LLM-driven coding workflows, providing language-specific Docker images and scripts to trigger commands inside them with full stdout/stderr passthrough.

## Images

| Image | Base | Tools |
|---|---|---|
| `cognition_runner/python:latest` | `python:3.12.9-slim` | `python`, `pytest`, `isort`, `flake8`, `black` |
| `cognition_runner/swift:latest` | `swift:5.10.1` | `swift build`, `swift test` |
| `cognition_runner/node:latest` | `node:20.18.3-slim` | `node`, `npm` |

All images include `git` and `pre-commit`. Base image versions are pinned to patch level for reproducibility.

## Scripts

- **`scripts/build.sh`** — builds all three images; respects `TAG_PREFIX` env var to override the default `cognition_runner/` namespace.
- **`scripts/run.sh`** — mounts the host working directory at `/workspace` and executes an arbitrary command inside the named container, inheriting the caller's stdout/stderr by default.

```bash
# Build all images
```

## What
Adds real-time typing indicators via WebSocket.

## How it works
Clients send a WebSocket message:
```json
{ "action": "typing", "channel_id": "...", "user_id": "...", "user_name": "Agent Name" }
```

All other clients subscribed to that channel receive:
```json
{ "type": "typing", "data": { "channel_id": "...", "user_id": "...", "user_name": "Agent Name" } }
```

## Details
- Ephemeral — no database storage, purely WebSocket-based
- Sender is excluded from receiving their own typing event
- Adds `broadcastToChannel()` utility for channel-scoped WebSocket delivery

author: jmmachacek
body:
Adds Exercise 5 to the GPU fundamentals workshop.

Exercise 5 uses warp shuffle plus a small shared buffer and one atomic operation per block. Each thread first computes a partial sum in a register with a grid-stride loop. A warp shuffle reduction (register-only, no shared memory) then gives one sum per warp in lane 0. Warp leaders write these warp sums into shared memory (one float per warp). The first warp reduces those values with another shuffle and writes the block sum to shared memory. The block leader performs a single atomic add to add that block sum into global memory.

The platform owner (`xdrivelogisticsltd@gmail.com`) was hitting the standard pending-approval wall because no mechanism existed to automatically assign the owner role — going through `/onboarding` would only ever create a `pending` broker or company_admin profile.

## Changes

### Middleware (`middleware.ts`)
- Added `OWNER_EMAIL` constant (env-var-overridable, defaults to `xdrivelogisticsltd@gmail.com`)
- Owner with `status='pending'` is let through — no approval needed
- Owner with no profile row (normally → `/onboarding`) is redirected straight to `/admin/approvals`

### DB migrations
- **`002_owner_always_active.sql`** — Trigger on `public.profiles` forces `status='active'` for any row where `role='owner'`; patches existing stale rows
- **`003_bootstrap_owner_by_email.sql`** — Owner email defined as a single `v_owner_email` constant; trigger on `auth.users` auto-creates `role='owner', status='active'` profile on sign-up; also runs an immediate upsert to fix any existing auth user with that email

```sql
-- Email literal appears once — trigger function is built dynamically
execute format($func$
  create or replace function public.auto_create_owner_profile()
  ...
  if lower(new.email) = lower(%L) then   -- owner email injected here
    insert into public.profiles ... values (new.id, 'owner', 'active', ...)
    on conflict (user_id) do update set role='owner', status='active', ...
  $func$, v_owner_email);
```

### Config

author: hoijnet
body:
# Support for range queries

This PR introduces ordered value navigation to WOQL through three new predicate
families: `triple_slice`, `triple_next`, and `triple_previous`, along with their
quad variants. These predicates exploit the sorted structure of the TerminusDB
value dictionary to perform range lookups in logarithmic time rather than
scanning every triple.

## Motivation

Selecting triples whose object falls within a value range (timestamps, numeric
thresholds, lexicographic intervals) previously required a full table scan with
Prolog-side filtering. On a 1M-triple dataset selecting 1,000 matching rows,
the indexed range query completes in under 3 ms while a full scan takes over
2 seconds, an improvement of roughly 800x. The gap widens linearly with dataset
size.

This is very useful for quickly scanning the timestamps of for example the commit log, and similar timestamped data. Selecting timestamps in a time range is now instant, only the two boundaries need to be identified (in logarithmic time), and then the values in the sequence are just iterated. 

## New WOQL predicates

| Predicate | Parameters | Description |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| `triple_slice` | `(Subject, Predicate, Object, Low, High)` | Select triples where Object is in [Low, High) |
| `quad_slice` | `(Subject, Predicate, Object, Low, High, Graph)` | Same, targeting a named graph |
| `triple_next` | `(Subject, Predicate, Object, Next)` | Find the next higher Object value for a given Subject/Predicate |
| `quad_next` | `(Subject, Predicate, Object, Next, Graph)` | Same, targeting a named graph |
| `triple_previous` | `(Subject, Predicate, Object, Previous)` | Find the next lower Object value for a given Subject/Predicate |
| `quad_previous` | `(Subject, Predicate, Object, Previous, Graph)` | Same, targeting a named graph |

For `triple_next` and `triple_previous`, either the Object or the Next/Previous
argument may be bound. The runtime dispatches the appropriate direction
automatically: if Object is ground it finds the neighbor in the named direction;
if the neighbor is ground it finds the Object in the reverse direction.

### WOQL JSON schema

`woql.json` gains `TripleSlice`, `TripleNext`, and `TriplePrevious` type
definitions with documentation, field metadata, mode annotations, and property
declarations. Quad equivalents are not added as they are Triple*** with the explicit graph.

### Client libraries

The JavaScript client (`woqlQuery.js`) and both Python clients
(`woql_query.py` in the main and community-fix repositories) add
`triple_slice`, `quad_slice`, `triple_next`, `quad_next`, `triple_previous`,
and `quad_previous` methods following the existing builder pattern.

## Benchmark results

All benchmarks use xsd:integer Unix timestamps on an in-memory store,
selecting 1,000 results from datasets of varying size.

| Triples | Range query | Full scan | Speedup |
|---------|------------|-----------|---------|
| 50,000 | 2.7 ms | 107 ms | 39x |
| 100,000 | 2.8 ms | 219 ms | 79x |
| 1,000,000 | 2.7 ms | 2.19 s | 807x |
| 10,000,000 | 2.9 ms | 22.5 s | 7,730x |

The range query time remains practically constant regardless of dataset size.

Greptile Summary

Enforced strict `dmPolicy=allowlist` behavior by preventing pairing-store entries from being merged into effective allowlists across all messaging channels (Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage, Telegram, LINE, and plugin extensions). Major changes: - `mergeAllowFromSources` and `resolveEffectiveAllowFromLists` now accept `dmPolicy` parameter and skip store entries when `dmPolicy === "allowlist"` - `resolveSenderCommandAuthorization` (plugin SDK) updated to gate store reads on `dmPolicy !== "allowlist"` - Applied consistently across 31 files covering core channels, extensions (MS Teams, Matrix, Feishu, Google Chat, IRC, Mattermost, Nextcloud Talk, BlueBubbles), and web access control - Comprehensive test coverage added for shared helpers, plugin SDK auth, WhatsApp access-control, and Discord component auth One issue found: - `resolveDmAllowState` in `src/security/dm-policy-shared.ts:80` doesn't respect `dmPolicy` when computing statistics for security audits, which could cause misleading audit reports when `dmPolicy=allowlist` but pairing-store entries exist

## **User description** ## Summary - The continuous damage factor was applied to `G_K`/`G` inside the stress component loop (`do i = strxb, strxe`), causing the shear modulus to be compounded by the damage factor on each iteration - With N stress components, this produced an effective `G_K * damage^N` instead of the intended `G_K * damage` - Fix moves the damage application before the loop in both cons-to-prim and prim-to-cons paths ## Test plan - [ ] Verify damage model test cases produce physically correct stress degradation - [ ] Golden file regeneration likely needed for damage model cases 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** **Apply damage factor once to shear modulus to stop exponential weakening** ### What Changed - The damage multiplier is applied a single time to the shear modulus before iterating stress components instead of being multiplied inside the component loop. - Shear contribution to pressure and elastic stress now uses the correctly degraded shear modulus rather than an N-times compounded reduction. - No change to user-facing inputs; results for damage-model cases will change to the physically intended stress degradation. ### Impact `✅ Correcter stress degradation for damage cases` `✅ Restored shear strength in damaged cells` `✅ Fewer unexpected differences in damage-model outputs`

author: burnoutberni
body:
This PR addresses a security vulnerability in the rate limiting middleware where the IP address was extracted from the *first* entry of the `X-Forwarded-For` header. This allowed attackers to bypass rate limits by sending a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` header (e.g., `X-Forwarded-For: spoofed-ip`).

The fix updates the logic to use the **last** IP in the `X-Forwarded-For` list, which corresponds to the client IP added by the trusted proxy (Caddy) in standard configurations. This ensures that the rate limiter uses the IP address verified by the proxy infrastructure.

**Changes:**
- `src/middleware/rateLimit.ts`: Changed IP extraction to `c.req.header('x-forwarded-for')?.split(',').pop()?.trim()`.
- `src/tests/middleware/rateLimit.security.test.ts`: Added a new test file that reproduces the vulnerability and verifies the fix.
- `.jules/sentinel.md`: Added a security journal entry documenting the vulnerability and the fix pattern.

**Verification:**
- A new test case `src/tests/middleware/rateLimit.security.test.ts` was added.
- The test simulates a request with `X-Forwarded-For: spoofed, real`.
- Before the fix, the rate limiter would count against `spoofed`.
- After the fix, the rate limiter counts against `real`, and blocks requests when the limit is exceeded for `real` IP, regardless of the `spoofed` IP.
- Ran `npm test src/tests/middleware/rateLimit.security.test.ts` to confirm it passes.
- Ran `npm test` to ensure no regressions.

body:
### Motivation
- Replace the legacy, minimal intervention abstraction with a richer interface that can declare stable id/version, arm parameters, and explicit policy descriptors for oracle, dependence, nullspec and output so real interventions can fully specify behavior and auditing data. 
- Ensure all intervention-declared descriptors are canonicalizable and bounded so arm assignment is fully auditable and deterministic across kernels. 
- Surface immutable, per-assignment audit material (intervention id/version, arm-parameters hash, descriptors) into ClaimCapsule and ETL so assignments are verifiable from capsule data alone.

### Description
- Replaced the old `EpistemicIntervention` surface with a new trait exposing `id`, `version`, `arm_parameters`, `oracle_policy`, `dependence_policy`, `nullspec_policy`, `output_policy`, `compute_k_charge` and `certification_barrier_multiplier`, and added `ChargeContext`, `KChargeResult`, and `BarrierContext` types. (core: `crates/evidenceos-core/src/trial/mod.rs`)
- Introduced structured policy descriptor types (`OraclePolicyDescriptor`, `DependencePolicyDescriptor`, `NullSpecPolicyDescriptor`, `OutputPolicyDescriptor`) and a canonicalization helper that reuses the existing canonical JSON machinery and enforces a bounded descriptor byte size. (core & daemon)
- At assignment time the router now computes and records deterministic audit material: `intervention_version`, `arm_parameters_hash` and the `descriptors` bundle; these fields are added to `TrialAssignment`, incorporated into the `trial_commitment_hash`, and persisted into `ClaimCapsule` and nested `trial` metadata so arm assignment is auditable from the capsule alone. (daemon: `crates/evidenceos-daemon/src/trial/mod.rs`, `crates/evidenceos-daemon/src/server/handlers_v2.rs`, `crates/evidenceos-daemon/src/server/mod.rs`, core: `crates/evidenceos-core/src/capsule.rs`)
- Extended ETL `ClaimSettlementEvent` to include optional `intervention_version` and `arm_parameters_hash` for continuity and backward compatibility, and updated tests to validate descriptor canonicalization stability and deterministic outputs. (core: `crates/evidenceos-core/src/etl.rs`, `crates/evidenceos-core/src/trial/tests.rs`)

### Testing
- Ran formatting check with `cargo fmt` which completed successfully. 
- Built the core crate with `cargo check -p evidenceos-core` which succeeded, and executed the core trial tests with `cargo test -p evidenceos-core trial:: -- --nocapture` which passed. 
- Attempted `cargo check -p evidenceos-core -p evidenceos-daemon`; this combined check encounters unrelated compile errors in other daemon modules (pre-existing borrow/mismatch issues) that are not caused by the intervention-interface changes. The change set itself compiles cleanly for the core crate and its new tests passed.

Story US-008: Response Caching System

## Story Description
Implement query hash-based caching for RAG responses. Cache key is normalized query hash (SHA-256). TTL configurable (default 24h). Track hit_count for analytics. Invalidate cache when new content is added. Implement manual cache clear endpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Cache stores response with query_hash key
2. Cache hit returns stored response
3. Cache expires after TTL
4. New content invalidates related cache entries
5. GET /api/admin/cache-stats returns hit rates
6. DELETE /api/admin/cache clears all cache
7. Typecheck passes
8. Tests for caching pass

## Changes
- Created  with:
  -  - SHA-256 hash of normalized query
  -  - retrieves cached response if not expired
  -  - stores response with TTL
  -  - clears all cache entries
  -  - alias for invalidateCache
  -  - returns hit rates and analytics
- Created  with:
  - GET /api/admin/cache-stats endpoint
  - DELETE /api/admin/cache endpoint
- Modified videos route to invalidate cache when new content is added
- Added comprehensive tests in 

## Tests
- generateQueryHash tests (consistent hash, different hashes for different queries)
- getCachedResponse tests (cache hit, cache miss, database error)
- cacheResponse tests (create new, update existing, error handling)
- invalidateCache tests (delete all, error handling)
- getCacheStats tests (correct statistics, empty cache, error handling)

body:
## Summary
This PR adds positioning controls to the existing Portal Names plugin so portal labels can be moved away from other portal overlays.

## What’s included
- New “Portal Names Opt” entry in the toolbox
- X/Y offset sliders (with persistence via localStorage)
- Optional dashed leader line from label to portal
- Optional highlight of the docking edge (only enabled when the leader line is on)
- Updated overlap/collision logic to account for the new label positioning

## Why
When other plugins render information on/near portals, portal names can become hard to read or visually merge with those overlays. Being able to offset labels makes the map much clearer while keeping the Portal Names layer simple and familiar.

## Notes
- Implemented as an update to the existing Portal Names plugin (not a separate plugin), since it’s a general usability feature.
- Backwards-compatible defaults: if offsets are left at 0 and the leader line is off, behavior matches the original plugin.

body:
Several correctness and quality issues identified in PR review: mismatched entity FK in budget lookup, missing daily check-in score award, wrong `ScoreChangeReason` for impulse buys, unconditional browser auto-launch, hardcoded publish path, inconsistent migration namespaces, and O(n²) waitlist loop.

## Data / Entity

- **`Budget.BucketId` FK**: Added `BucketId` + `Bucket?` navigation property to `Budget` entity and `BudgetConfiguration`. `GetMonthlyLimitAsync` was querying `b.CategoryId == bucketId` — a category/bucket identity mix-up that silently returned wrong overrides. Now queries `b.BucketId == bucketId`. Migration `AddBudgetBucketId` included.
- **`BudgetService.UpdateAsync`**: Persists `BucketId` alongside existing fields.

## Scoring

- **Daily check-in**: `ProcessDailyCheckInAsync` now awards `+2` via `ScoreChangeReason.DailyCheckIn` on every new check-in (first-time and subsequent), guarded against double-award when already checked in today.
- **Impulse buy reason**: Added `ImpulseBuy = 9` to `ScoreChangeReason`. Impulse penalty in `ScoringService` was using `OverBudget`, making event filtering/reporting incorrect.

```csharp
// Before
ScoreChangeReason.OverBudget, "Impulse purchase recorded"

// After
ScoreChangeReason.ImpulseBuy, "Impulse purchase recorded"
```

## Startup / Config

- **Browser auto-launch**: Wrapped in `if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())` — was firing unconditionally in production/containers.
- **Publish path**: Replaced hardcoded `F:\Repos\CoinStack` with `$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)\publish`.

## Migrations

- Standardised `AddTransactionAutoDeductFields` and `SnapshotSync` to `FinanceManager.Data.Migrations` namespace — they were the only two using `CoinStack.Data.Migrations`.

## Performance

- **`WaitlistService`**: Converted `monthlyExpenses` list to `Dictionary<int, decimal>` before the bucket loop — was O(buckets × expenses), now O(buckets).

body:
## 🎰 Integração com Backend Casino-API

### Resumo
Esta PR implementa a integração completa do frontend com o backend NestJS (casino-api).

### Mudanças

#### Novos Serviços Criados
- **`wallet.ts`** - Operações de carteira (saldo, conversão de valores)
- **`payments.ts`** - Depósitos PIX e saques (usando endpoints corretos)
- **`games.ts`** - Lista de jogos do backend com fallback
- **`tenants.ts`** - Configurações multi-tenant (tema, cores, PWA)
- **`index.ts`** - Exportação centralizada de todos os serviços

#### Atualizações
- **`api.ts`** - Adicionados interceptors para:
  - Token JWT automático
  - Header `x-tenant-domain` para multi-tenancy
  - Tratamento de erros global (401, 403, 500, etc.)
  - Timeout de 30s

- **`wallet/page.tsx`** - Corrigido para usar:
  - `/transactions/withdraw` (em vez de `/payments/withdraw`)
  - Saldo real da API
  - Tratamento de erros melhorado

### Endpoints do Backend Mapeados
| Serviço | Endpoint | Descrição |
|---------|----------|-----------|
| Auth | `POST /auth/login` | Login |
| Auth | `POST /auth/register` | Registro |
| Auth | `GET /auth/me` | Perfil do usuário |
| Wallet | `GET /wallets/me/balance` | Saldo da carteira |
| Transactions | `POST /transactions/deposit` | Criar depósito |
| Transactions | `POST /transactions/withdraw` | Criar saque |
| Payments | `POST /payments/deposit` | Depósito PIX (QR Code) |
| Benefits | `GET /benefits/status` | Status dos benefícios |
| Benefits | `POST /benefits/claim/:type` | Resgatar benefício |
| Games | `GET /games/top` | Jogos em destaque |
| Tenants | `GET /public/tenants/:domain/config` | Config do tenant |

### Como Testar
1. Configure `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` no `.env.local` (ou use o padrão)
2. Faça login com um usuário válido
3. Teste depósito/saque na página de carteira
4. Verifique o saldo sendo atualizado

### Backend Reference
- Repositório: https://github.com/franklinprotazio/casino-api/
- Framework: NestJS com Prisma
- Porta padrão: 3001
